author: marcusotter
body:
Some much needed maintenance

Functional changes
- djs upgraded
- Prints how long the bot has been offline on startup
- Only caches 1 item per guild instead of 5, hopefully improves ever growing RAM. Worst case we have to set it to 0 and pray at some point.
- Do not log X threads created in the past minute twice
- Uses PinMessages permission instead of ManageMessages to pin message.
- Stops using some deprecated stuff in djs

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR fixes issues where `npm test` could hang or log errors due to incomplete mocks.

1.  **Fixed WebSpeechProvider Timeout:** The `WebSpeechProvider` waits 1 second for voices to load if `getVoices()` returns an empty array. The global test setup now returns dummy voices, eliminating this delay and potential hang risk across all tests using TTS.
2.  **Fixed ReaderView Mock:** `ReaderView` accesses `rendition.hooks.content.register`, which was undefined in the `epub.js` mock. This caused `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` in tests. The mock in `ReaderView.test.tsx` has been updated to include the `hooks` object.

These changes ensure the test suite runs reliably and faster.

author: m4rcusml
body:
This pull request introduces a manual bill creation flow (without requiring an image upload) and refactors both backend and frontend to support this feature. It also restructures the frontend navigation for bill creation, adds new screens for participant setup, and improves validation and user experience for bill creation.

**Backend changes for manual bill creation:**

* Added support for creating bills without an image: `imageUrl` and `imageKey` fields in the `Bill` model are now optional (`String?`), and the backend allows bill creation without a file upload. The bill is immediately set to `DIVIDING` status and can include participant count, bill name, and service fee. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-93ead908b5ffa6f6e995757b3739fb02b4e9f8d0ea1da0ec34a9c03c1a33f9bfL67-R68) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-dfd169a34cdb155920cdde66232687ef1428b456a1611aeae3df052ccd4b828bL32-R36) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-84e67bbf27b80190b7feb645bba411d084b63eec8f44ad07e0e51ba5dfbd1f94L26-R31) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-84e67bbf27b80190b7feb645bba411d084b63eec8f44ad07e0e51ba5dfbd1f94R68-R102) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-de930bf2bf48a53a9e80261294dd272346533e4cdc8c0a76a932aaebe36d1ca0L1-R24)
* Updated service logic to handle optional image fields for generating signed URLs and deleting images only if present. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-84e67bbf27b80190b7feb645bba411d084b63eec8f44ad07e0e51ba5dfbd1f94L174-R214) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-84e67bbf27b80190b7feb645bba411d084b63eec8f44ad07e0e51ba5dfbd1f94L226-R269)

**Frontend changes for bill creation flow:**

* Refactored navigation: Bill creation steps are now under a new `(create)` route group with a custom stack layout, separating screens for new bill setup, participant entry, and camera scanning. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-97ef0a87c2ad8d976240ac9ad693da46c5d22d37a90902ea25de012786f2073eR1-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6417007cb8e84ff2fcdb11d052a13bfb130fa9314ab9304139ef199babe34ff9L2-R16)
* Added `new.tsx` screen for manual bill setup, including participant count, optional bill name, and service fee, with improved validation using `zod` and `react-hook-form`.
* Added `participants.tsx` screen for entering participant names before scanning, with UI to add/remove names and validation for participant limits.
* Updated camera screen import paths due to route restructuring.
* Changed login redirect to point to the new camera flow.

**Backend DTO validation improvements:**

* Enhanced `CreateBillDto` with new fields (`billName`, `participantCount`, `serviceFeePercentage`) and validation rules for participant count and service fee percentage.

author: copilot
body:
Complete redesign of AI & IoT presentation (`lab3/index.html`) with enhanced cyberpunk/Matrix aesthetic and dual-mode navigation system separating main content (12 slides) from interactive demos (5 hidden slides).

## Navigation Architecture

**Main slides (1-12):** Standard presentation flow with arrow keys, PREV/NEXT buttons, progress counter showing `X / 12`, and mini-map dots.

**Hidden slides (13-17):** Popup-style demos accessible from menu cards. Navigation controls hidden, ESC key returns to menu, back buttons on each slide. Click outside slide area returns to menu.

```javascript
// Navigation mode switching based on slide index
function updateSlideDisplay() {
    const navControls = document.querySelector('.nav-controls');
    const isHiddenSlide = currentSlideIndex > mainSlides;
    
    if (isHiddenSlide) {
        navControls.style.display = 'none';  // Hide nav for demos
    } else {
        navControls.style.display = 'flex';
        // Standard navigation updates...
    }
}
```

## Visual Design System

- **Slide 1:** HUD header (ROOT_ACCESS, CPU/MEM bars, ID badge), terminal output left, ASCII art right, system warning banner
- **Slide 2:** 4 menu cards routing to hidden slides: AI Demo → 13, Mirai Simulator → 15, Ukraine Map → 17, Security Checklist → 16
- **Slide 4:** AI technology cards with ID badges (GPT-4, MJ-V6, COPILOT, red THREAT badge for Deepfake)
- **Slide 7:** War tech statistics grid (Drones 10k+, Starlink 42k+, 95% defense success rate)
- **Slide 12:** Large VAR_A/B/C quiz cards with percentage displays
- **Slide 17:** Real Ukraine SVG contour with animated attack/defense points, filters by year (2022/2023/2024), statistics: 8,400+ attacks, 95% defended

Corner decorations (cyan/pink L-brackets) on all slides. Grid background with scanline animation. Glitch effects on headers. Neon color scheme via CSS variables.

## Interactive Features

Hidden slides provide hands-on demos:
- **Slide 13:** AI hallucination generator with example responses
- **Slide 14:** 5-question IoT security quiz with scoring
- **Slide 15:** Mirai botnet attack simulator with 4-stage animation
- **Slide 16:** Router security checklist with localStorage persistence
- **Slide 17:** Ukraine cyber defense map with year filters and real statistics

## Завдання

Повністю переробити презентацію в `lab3/index.html`, використовуючи дизайн з файлу `Genspark (02.12.2025 18：19：47) (2).html` який знаходиться в цьому ж репозиторії.

### ПРИХОВАНІ СЛАЙДИ (13-17) - НЕ в прогрес-барі

author: rshade
body:
This PR implements E2E test support features to facilitate integration testing with `pulumicost-core`. It introduces a "Test Mode" and validation logic for expected cost ranges, fulfilling the requirements of issue #26.

## Summary

- Add test mode detection via `PULUMICOST_TEST_MODE=true` environment variable
- Define expected cost ranges for t3.micro EC2 and gp2 EBS in us-east-1
- Add validation helpers for cost tolerance checking
- Enhance debug logging when test mode is enabled

## Implementation Details

### New Files

- `internal/plugin/testmode.go` - Test mode detection and env validation
- `internal/plugin/testmode_test.go` - Unit tests for test mode (14 cases)
- `internal/plugin/expected.go` - Expected cost ranges and validation helpers
- `internal/plugin/expected_test.go` - Unit tests for expected costs (22 cases)

### Modified Files

- `internal/plugin/plugin.go` - Added `testMode` field and initialization
- `internal/plugin/projected.go` - Enhanced debug logging in test mode
- `cmd/pulumicost-plugin-aws-public/main.go` - Startup validation call
- `README.md` - E2E test support documentation
- `CLAUDE.md` - Feature documentation

### Key Functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `IsTestMode()` | Returns true when `PULUMICOST_TEST_MODE=true` | | `ValidateTestModeEnv()` | Logs warning for invalid env values | | `GetExpectedRange()` | Lookup expected cost for resource type/sku/region | | `IsWithinTolerance()` | Check if actual cost is within tolerance | | `CalculateExpectedActualCost()` | Compute prorated actual cost |

## Test Plan

- [x] `make lint` passes (0 issues)
- [x] `make test` passes (all tests)
- [x] Coverage above 80% (81.3%)
- [x] `npx markdownlint-cli README.md` passes
- [x] Test mode disabled by default (zero overhead)
- [x] Backward compatible with existing tests

## Expected Cost Ranges

Reference values for E2E test validation (as of 2025-12-01):

| Resource | SKU | Region | Monthly | Tolerance |
|----------|-----|--------|---------|-----------|
| EC2 | t3.micro | us-east-1 | $7.592 | ±1% |
| EBS | gp2 (8GB) | us-east-1 | $0.80 | ±5% |

## Known Limitations

- Expected cost ranges currently only defined for us-east-1
- Only t3.micro and gp2 have reference values; other resources return not-found

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a purely additive change with zero overhead when test mode is disabled.

Closes #26

author: copilot
body:
Workflow run #19879014217 failed because user entered URL in title field and title in URL field. Script validation correctly rejected the non-URL value.

### Changes

Added auto-detection to swap fields when title contains URL pattern but target URL doesn't:

```javascript
const urlPattern = /^https?:\/\/.+/i;
const titleLooksLikeUrl = urlPattern.test(title);
const targetUrlLooksLikeUrl = urlPattern.test(targetUrl);

if (titleLooksLikeUrl && !targetUrlLooksLikeUrl) {
  [targetUrl, title] = [title, targetUrl];
}
```

Applied to both `process-response` and `process-bookmark` workflows for consistency.

### Edge cases
- Both fields contain URLs → no swap (validation handles downstream)
- Neither field contains URL → no swap (validation handles downstream)
- Correctly ordered fields → no swap

author: youcanbe0101
body:
## Summary
This PR implements an automated system to collect and track AWS re:Invent 2025 updates, announcements, and blog posts from official AWS sources.

## Requirements Implemented

### Core Functionality
- ✅ **Automated Data Collection**: Fetches announcements and updates from AWS re:Invent 2025 official sources
  - Primary source: AWS blog at https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/category/events/reinvent/
  - Additional AWS news pages support
- ✅ **Data Extraction**: Extracts relevant information including:
  - Announcement titles
  - Publication dates
  - Descriptions/summaries
  - URLs
  - Categories
- ✅ **Structured Data Storage**: Stores collected data in structured formats (JSON and CSV)
  - Fields: title, date, summary, URL, and category
- ✅ **Automated Scheduling**: Implements periodic checking for new updates
  - Configurable check intervals
  - Background scheduler support
- ✅ **Error Handling**: Gracefully handles unavailable sources
  - Retry logic with exponential backoff
  - Comprehensive error logging
- ✅ **Manual Execution**: Provides simple way to run collection manually
  - Command-line interface
  - Shell scripts for easy execution
- ✅ **Comprehensive Documentation**: Includes setup, configuration, and usage guides

### Key Features
- **Multiple Data Formats**: Supports both JSON and CSV export
- **Configurable Settings**: JSON-based configuration for easy customization
- **Shell Scripts**: Convenient scripts for manual collection and scheduled runs
- **Progress Tracking**: Real-time collection progress indicators
- **Data Deduplication**: Prevents duplicate entries across collection runs

## Files Added

### Core Implementation
- **`reinvent_collector.py`**: Main collection script with web scraping and data extraction logic
- **`scheduler.py`**: Automated scheduling system for periodic updates
- **`config.json`**: Configuration file for URLs, intervals, and data paths

### Documentation
- **`README.md`**: Comprehensive setup and usage guide
- **`AWS_REINVENT_2025_UPDATES.md`**: Detailed requirements and implementation documentation
- **`QUICKSTART.md`**: Quick setup guide for immediate use
- **`PROJECT_SUMMARY.txt`**: Project overview and technical details
- **`VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST.md`**: Testing and validation checklist

### Utilities
- **`requirements.txt`**: Python dependencies (requests, beautifulsoup4, schedule)
- **`run_collection.sh`**: Shell script for manual collection
- **`run_scheduler.sh`**: Shell script for starting scheduled collection
- **`.gitignore`**: Excludes Python cache, virtual environments, and data files

body:
## Summary

Implements the **Future Credit Card Statements** feature (spec 023), allowing users to pre-define future credit card statement balances for better cashflow projection accuracy.

## User Stories Implemented

### US1: Add Future Statement to Credit Card (P1 - MVP) ✅
- Users can add future statement balances via a form with month/year selector
- Pre-fills with the next logical month
- Shows warning dialog when adding for current month (FR-011)
- Cashflow projection uses future statements for future months, 0 if not defined (FR-006)

### US2: Edit or Delete Future Statement (P2) ✅
- Edit mode in the form with pre-populated values
- Delete button with confirmation dialog
- Past months are not editable (disabled state)

### US3: Automatic Statement Progression (P3) ✅
- On app launch, checks if month has changed since last visit
- Promotes future statements to current `statementBalance`
- Handles multi-month catch-up for users who haven't logged in
- Cleans up past-month statements (FR-012)

### US4: View Upcoming Statement Schedule (P4) ✅
- Collapsible "Próximas Faturas" section on credit card cards
- Statement count badge on the trigger
- Chronologically sorted (nearest first)
- Proper month/year formatting (e.g., "Janeiro/2025")

## Technical Changes

### Database
- New `future_statements` table with:
  - Unique constraint on `(credit_card_id, target_month, target_year)`
  - RLS policies for household-scoped security
  - Realtime subscription enabled
  - Cascade delete on credit card deletion (FR-010)

### Store & Hooks
- Added `futureStatements` state to finance store
- Implemented CRUD actions: `addFutureStatement`, `updateFutureStatement`, `deleteFutureStatement`
- Added Realtime subscription for `future_statements` table
- Created `useMonthProgression` hook for automatic progression

### Cashflow Engine
- Modified `getCreditCardAmountForDate` to:
  - Use `statementBalance` for current/past months
  - Lookup future statement for future months
  - Return 0 if no future statement defined (FR-006)

### UI Components
- `FutureStatementForm` - Add/edit form with validation
- `FutureStatementList` - List with empty state CTA
- `Collapsible` - Custom collapsible component
- Updated `CreditCardCard` with new section

## Files Changed

- `src/stores/preferences-store.ts` - `lastProgressionCheck` preference

body:
## Summary

This PR optimizes gas usage in the pool package through two main improvements:
1. Replacing `ufmt.Sprintf` calls with direct string concatenation
2. Replacing AVL tree with native Gno `map` for pool storage

## Changes

### Phase 1: String Concatenation Optimization
- **pool/utils.gno**: Replaced `ufmt.Sprintf` with string concatenation in `GetPoolPath`
- **pool/v1/position.gno**: Replaced `ufmt.Sprintf` with string concatenation in `getPositionKey`

### Phase 2: Data Structure Optimization (AVL Tree → Map)
- **pool/types.gno**: Updated `IPoolStore` interface to use `map[string]*Pool` instead of `*avl.Tree`
- **pool/store.gno**: Implemented map-based storage operations
- **pool/v1/init.gno**: Changed initialization to use map literals
- **pool/v1/manager.gno**: Updated pool operations to use native map access
- **pool/v1/getter.gno**: Simplified pool lookups with map access
- **pool/v1/api.gno**: Updated API methods to use map operations
- **pool/v1/assert.gno**: Updated pool existence checks
- **mock/pool_store.gno**: Updated mock implementation to match new interface
- **Test files**: Updated all test files to use map syntax

### Cyclic Import Fix
- **pool/_helper_test.gno**: Removed mock import to break cyclic dependency
- **pool/_mock_test.gno**: Copied MockResponse locally to avoid mock dependency
- **pool/v1/manager.gno**: Added nil check for pools map initialization
- **test/fuzz/_mock_test.gno**: Updated to properly import and use pool types

## Performance Improvements

### Full Comparison: Baseline (94d46728) vs Current (4a780246)

This comparison shows the total impact of all optimizations combined.

#### 🎯 Major Gas Improvements

| Operation | Baseline (94d46728) | Current (4a780246) | Improvement | % Reduction |
|-----------|---------------------|---------------------|-------------|-------------|
| **CreatePool (wugnot:gns:500)** | 9,421,068 | 6,980,874 | **-2,440,194** | **-25.9%** 🔥 |
| **CreatePool (wugnot:gns:3000)** | 9,423,206 | 6,982,779 | **-2,440,427** | **-25.9%** 🔥 |
| **Position Decrease Liquidity** | 17,748,168 | 14,286,184 | **-3,461,984** | **-19.5%** 🔥 |
| **Position Increase Liquidity** | 12,885,128 | 11,334,089 | **-1,551,039** | **-12.0%** |
| **Position Mint** | 32,077,387 | 30,371,770 | **-1,705,617** | **-5.3%** |
| **Mint Position (fee:3000)** | 29,411,640 | 27,705,377 | **-1,706,263** | **-5.8%** |

#### Swap Operations

| Operation | Baseline (94d46728) | Current (4a780246) | Improvement | % Reduction |
|-----------|---------------------|---------------------|-------------|-------------|
| **ExactOutSwapRoute (gns→wugnot)** | 21,894,791 | 21,109,074 | -785,717 | -3.6% |
| **ExactOutSwapRoute (wugnot→gns)** | 13,279,805 | 12,481,086 | -798,719 | -6.0% |
| **Router Exact Out Swap Route** | 30,809,715 | 30,049,875 | -759,840 | -2.5% |
| **Router Exact Out Single Swap** | 31,363,368 | 30,130,997 | -1,232,371 | -3.9% |

#### 💾 Storage Improvements

| Operation | Baseline | Current | Improvement |
|-----------|----------|---------|-------------|
| **CreatePool (wugnot:gns:500)** | 17,829 bytes | 16,942 bytes | **-887 bytes (-5.0%)** |
| **CreatePool (wugnot:gns:3000)** | 17,830 bytes | 16,943 bytes | **-887 bytes (-5.0%)** |

#### ⚡ CPU Cycles Improvements

| Operation | Baseline (94d46728) | Current (4a780246) | Improvement | % Reduction |
|-----------|---------------------|---------------------|-------------|-------------|
| **CreatePool (wugnot:gns:500)** | 3,102,628 | 2,518,498 | **-584,130** | **-18.8%** |
| **CreatePool (wugnot:gns:3000)** | 3,104,734 | 2,520,387 | **-584,347** | **-18.8%** |
| **Position Decrease Liquidity** | 14,958,221 | 11,605,125 | **-3,353,096** | **-22.4%** |
| **Position Increase Liquidity** | 11,809,699 | 10,285,882 | **-1,523,817** | **-12.9%** |
| **Position Mint** | 22,212,424 | 20,566,989 | **-1,645,435** | **-7.4%** |

### Phase Breakdown

#### Phase 1: String Concatenation (94d46728 → 4ed8e565)
String concatenation with the `+` operator is approximately **4x cheaper** than `ufmt.Sprintf` in terms of CPU cycles.

- Position Decrease Liquidity: -864,220 CPU cycles (-5.8%)
- Position operations: 1-6% improvement
- Total CPU cycles saved: ~1.9M across major operations

#### Phase 2: AVL Tree → Map (3824cdf1 → 13d7996a)
Replacing AVL tree with native Go map improves performance from **O(log n) to O(1)** for pool lookups and insertions.

- CreatePool: ~1.86M gas saved (~21% reduction)
- Storage: -887 bytes per pool
- Algorithm complexity: O(log n) → O(1)

### Key Highlights

🎯 **CreatePool Operations**: Up to **25.9% gas reduction** (2.44M gas saved)  
⚡ **Position Operations**: Up to **19.5% gas reduction** (3.46M gas saved)  
💾 **Storage Efficiency**: **887 bytes saved** per pool creation  
📊 **CPU Performance**: Up to **22.4% CPU cycles reduction**  
🏗️ **Code Quality**: Simpler codebase with native data structures  
🔄 **Scalability**: Performance improves as pool count increases (O(1) vs O(log n))  

### Overall Impact

Combined optimizations result in:
- **Up to 26% gas reduction** for pool creation operations
- **Up to 22% CPU cycles reduction** for position operations
- **~5% storage reduction** per pool
- **Simplified codebase** with removal of AVL tree complexity
- **Better performance scalability** as the number of pools grows
- **No breaking changes** to the public API

### Testing

- ✅ All unit tests passing
- ✅ All integration tests passing
- ✅ Fuzz tests passing
- ✅ Cyclic import issues resolved

author: soradotwav
body:
### Summary
Replaces the rough heuristic token estimation (`length / 4`) with a real BPE tokenizer using `js-tiktoken`. This provides users with exact token counts (using the `cl100k_base` encoding), ensuring their context bundles fit within GPT-4 and Claude context windows.

### Changes
- **Added `js-tiktoken`:** utilized the `lite` version to minimize package footprint.
- **Implemented Lazy Loading:** The tokenizer ranks (`cl100k_base`) are loaded via dynamic import in the background. This ensures the CLI startup time remains instant (`fullsend --help` doesn't lag) while the heavy lifting happens during the file scan.
- **Updated CLI Output:** Now displays "Tokens (GPT-4/Claude): X" instead of a tilde estimate.

### Performance
- Usage of `import()` inside `lib/token-counter.js` prevents the main thread from blocking on startup.
- The tokenizer is warmed up immediately upon module import, so it's ready by the time the directory scan completes.

### Testing
Verified manually with a single file containing "hello":
- **Old behavior:** ~2 tokens (heuristic)
- **New behavior:** 22 tokens (1 for content + 21 for markdown wrapper overhead).
- This confirms we are counting the *actual* payload sent to the LLM.

This pull request introduces comprehensive documentation and a project rebranding for the Python Template Server. The changes focus on improving developer onboarding, clarifying architecture and workflows, and providing detailed API and operational documentation. Key updates include a new project overview, expanded README, and dedicated API documentation.

**Project Documentation & Developer Experience**

* Added `.github/copilot-instructions.md` with a thorough project overview, architecture breakdown, developer workflows, Docker build details, code conventions, security patterns, and CI/CD requirements. This document serves as an in-depth guide for new contributors and maintainers.

These changes collectively make the repository much more accessible and production-ready for developers looking to build secure and observable FastAPI applications.

author: daturkel
body:
## Summary

- Simplified formatter API by replacing two confusing parameters with a single `blank_lines` parameter
- Enhanced `auto` mode to keep comments grouped with their associated labels
- Achieved 100% test coverage across the entire codebase

## Changes

**API Simplification:**
- Replaced `blank_line_before_label` (bool) and `preserve_newlines` (bool) with `blank_lines: Literal["auto", "preserve", "none"]`
- Default is now `"preserve"` to follow principle of least surprise
- CLI flag changed from `--no-blank-line-before-label` and `--preserve-newlines` to `--blank-lines {auto,preserve,none}`

**Modes:**
- `"preserve"`: Preserve blank lines from source (previous `preserve_newlines=True`)
- `"auto"`: Add blank lines before labels, keeping comments grouped with labels
- `"none"`: No automatic blank lines (previous `blank_line_before_label=False`)

**Enhanced auto mode:**
When adding blank lines before labels, comments immediately preceding a label now stay grouped with it:
```python
# Before (comments separated from labels):
NOOP
; foo
label:

# After with blank_lines="auto" (comments grouped with labels):
NOOP

; foo
label:
```

**Test Coverage:**
- Added tests for `BlankLine` class methods (`__str__`, `__repr__`, `__eq__`)
- Added tests for comment grouping behavior in auto mode
- All 460 tests passing with 100% coverage

## Test Plan
- [x] All existing tests updated and passing (460 tests)
- [x] New tests for BlankLine coverage
- [x] New tests for comment grouping in auto mode
- [x] 100% code coverage achieved

author: mathisverstrepen
body:
This pull request introduces a new feature that allows users to regenerate the title of a graph using either the first prompt node or all prompt nodes, improving the flexibility and accuracy of graph naming. The changes span backend and frontend code, adding new API endpoints, streaming logic, and UI components to support this functionality.

### Backend: Graph Title Regeneration

* Added two new async functions, `get_all_nodes_of_type_in_graph` and `get_root_nodes_of_type`, to `database/neo4j/crud.py` for efficiently retrieving prompt nodes from a graph, supporting both "all" and "first" strategies.
* Implemented `regenerate_title_stream` in `services/stream.py`, which streams the regenerated title to the frontend based on the selected strategy, using the graph's prompt node(s) and an LLM.
* Integrated the new title regeneration stream into the chat websocket endpoint, enabling clients to request title regeneration via a dedicated message type. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bc5b462155ce968d7a09eeb20de3eb2f7921abdb13ae4237a054f98dcb3f133aR102-R125) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bc5b462155ce968d7a09eeb20de3eb2f7921abdb13ae4237a054f98dcb3f133aL24-R24)

### Frontend: UI Integration and Event Handling

* Added a "Regenerate Title" submenu to the sidebar graph actions menu, allowing users to trigger title regeneration for either the first prompt node or all prompt nodes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0d3b55fd6f5ad7a30e135127d8e161f7fbeb7664d703e34ee26775492bf00737R23-R58) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0d3b55fd6f5ad7a30e135127d8e161f7fbeb7664d703e34ee26775492bf00737L59-L148)
* Updated sidebar components to handle the new `regenerate-title` event, ensuring the UI reflects the title regeneration process and updates the graph name accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a1eed58923165d579f5f65ccac3b7ed2a1f053a60ee614fcf29ad358ef58743dR323-R330) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a1eed58923165d579f5f65ccac3b7ed2a1f053a60ee614fcf29ad358ef58743dR471) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a1eed58923165d579f5f65ccac3b7ed2a1f053a60ee614fcf29ad358ef58743dR500) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a1eed58923165d579f5f65ccac3b7ed2a1f053a60ee614fcf29ad358ef58743dR530) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a1eed58923165d579f5f65ccac3b7ed2a1f053a60ee614fcf29ad358ef58743dR557)

These changes collectively enhance the user experience by providing more control over graph naming and ensuring seamless backend/frontend integration for title regeneration requests.

author: hmhealey
body:
#### Summary
Tracking `caretPosition` in the AdvancedTextEditor's state on every mouse up or key up and attempting to sync its value back to the input started causing problems since we upgraded to React 18 which incude breaking the spell checker in Chrome/Desktop on Windows (MM-66659) and causing the keyboard cursor to move around weirdly while typing in the thread popout (MM-66832 and potentially #34552). The reason that that causes bugs seems to be due to a race condition between the `useEffect` that updates the textarea based on `caretPosition` and the event handler that calls `setCaretPosition`.

While React 18 seems to have made this an issue for the spell checker, I think that that may have been a potential issue even before we upgraded React. The fact that the thread popout is more affected by this would indicate that perhaps the fact that main app isn't as affected by it because it runs a bit slower than the popout. It's possible that `caretPosition` is actually the cause of the "slow typing" bugs we fought with years ago because that's been in the component state since https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost-webapp/pull/3546 back in 2019.

To fix that, I got rid of the state and replaced everywhere we used it by just having them access the textarea's `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` directly. We only ever used it for specific one-off actions (like adding an emoji or the formatting buttons), so it doesn't need to be in the React state. This also means that we have a single source of truth for the actual location of the keyboard caret.

While making those changes, I ended up making some additional changes to `useEditorEmojiPicker` to have it use `execCommand('insertText')` which has the additional benefit of preserving the undo/redo stack when adding an emoji using the emoji picker. Ensuring that change was unit tested got a bit out of hand, but I'm still happy with the result.

See individual commits for more details.

#### Ticket Link
MM-66659
MM-66832

#### Release Note
```release-note
- Improved performance of the post textbox and fixed typing bugs in the thread popout
- Fixed bug where Chrome/Desktop App spell check on Windows often couldn't correct typos
```

author: vegetarianorc
body:
## What was changed

- Add support for acquiring and using a `MetricMeter` inside Nexus operation handlers.
- :boom: Narrow the accepted type of executor for sync Nexus operations from `concurrent.futures.Executor` to `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`. This is a breaking change.

## Why?

To enable users to create metrics in Nexus operations in the same way as Activities.

The type of executor was narrowed to prevent users from running into known issues around pickleability. Additionally, handling Nexus operation start/cancel requests are intended to be short and aren't a great fit for something like a `ProcessPoolExecutor`.

## Checklist



### How was this tested:

New tests were added to include execution of Nexus operations via the async event loop and a `ThreadPoolExecutor` and verify that metrics are sent. The new tests mirror the existing workflow metrics tests, but are skipped in the time skipping environment due to lack of Nexus support.

This PR adds support for automatic Traditional Chinese to Simplified Chinese conversion using `opencc`.

author: erickgross-19
body:
- Add bifurcation parameters to SpaceColonizationParams:
  - encourage_bifurcation: bool to enable feature (default False)
  - min_attractions_for_bifurcation: minimum attraction points needed (default 3)
  - max_children_per_node: maximum children to create (default 2)
  - bifurcation_angle_threshold_deg: minimum angle spread to trigger (default 40°)
  - bifurcation_probability: probability when conditions met (default 0.7)

- Implement bifurcation logic:
  - Compute angle spread of attraction vectors
  - If conditions met (count >= min AND spread >= threshold), cluster attractions
  - Use angle-based two-means clustering to group attractions
  - Compute Murray's law radii for children: r_i = r_parent * (w_i/Σw_j)^(1/3)
  - Grow each child toward its cluster centroid
  - Fall back to single-child growth if radii below minimum

- Add helper functions:
  - _compute_angle_spread(): compute max pairwise angle between vectors
  - _cluster_attractions_by_angle(): angle-based clustering
  - _apply_directional_blending(): extracted directional constraint logic

- Backward compatible: defaults to single-child growth (encourage_bifurcation=False)

Requested by user to encourage max children per node instead of linear growth

body:
Implements a comprehensive legal search system that queries multiple AI models in parallel (DeepSeek, Grok, Kimi), extracts legal entities, validates source attribution, and synthesizes consensus while flagging contradictions. Integrates with all legal functions (consultation, FOIA, complaints, petitions) to eliminate AI hallucinations.

## Core System (`enhancedLegalSearch.ts`)

**Entity Extraction Engine** - 6 entity types with regex patterns:
- Dates (3 formats), Statutes (U.S.C., state codes, all 27 amendments)
- Citations (Supreme Court, circuits, case names), Parties (officers, departments)
- Constitutional clauses, Courts (all levels)

**Source Attribution Validator** - Strict validation:
- Only accepts URLs, statute citations (42 U.S.C. § 1983), case law (490 U.S. 386)
- Filters hedging language, discards unsourced facts
- Public API: `validateFact(fact, sources)` returns `{valid, reason}`

**Consensus Synthesis Engine**:
- Groups similar facts (60% Jaccard similarity)
- Identifies contradictions (date mismatches, conflicting claims)
- Deduplicates while aggregating sources
- Confidence scoring: 0.80 base + 0.05 per model agreement, capped at 1.0

**Timeline & Categorization**:
- Chronological timeline from parsed dates
- 6-dimension sorting: relevance, recency, authority, jurisdiction, party, document type

## Integration Points

Added enhanced search functions to 4 modules:

```typescript
// legalAI.ts
const result = await analyzeLegalIssueWithEnhancedSearch(description, state);
// Returns: { analysis, searchResults, verifiedFacts, timeline, discrepancies }

// foiaRoutingSystem.ts
const { foia, legalResearch } = await generateEnhancedFOIAWithSearch(foiaData);

// complaintDraftingSystem.ts
const { complaint, legalResearch, verifiedFacts } = await generateEnhancedComplaintWithSearch(data);

// petitionService.ts
const { petitionContent, legalResearch, verifiedFacts } = await generateEnhancedPetitionWithSearch(workflow);
```

Each enhanced function:
- Performs parallel AI queries via `Promise.allSettled()`
- Extracts entities from all responses
- Validates source attribution
- Synthesizes consensus with discrepancy detection
- Falls back to standard generation on failure

## Error Handling

- 36 try-catch blocks across 5 modules
- 52 fallback mechanisms (OpenRouter → unified AI provider)
- Circuit breaker pattern for failed models
- Comprehensive logging at each pipeline stage

## Example Output

```typescript
{
  attributedFacts: [
    {
      fact: "42 U.S.C. § 1983 provides civil action for deprivation of rights",
      sources: ["https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1983"],
      confidence: 0.95,
      extractedFrom: "DeepSeek, Grok",
      verified: true,
      entities: [{ type: 'statute', value: '42 U.S.C. § 1983', jurisdiction: 'Federal' }]
    }
  ],
  discrepancies: [
    {
      type: 'date_mismatch',
      description: "Different dates reported: 2023-01-15 vs 2023-02-01",
      severity: 'high'
    }
  ]
}
```

## Technical Notes

- Entity extraction: 95%+ confidence scoring with context windows
- Amendment pattern: Covers all 27 amendments (First through Twenty-Seventh)
- Case citations: Flexible pattern handles with/without reporters (U.S., F.2d, F.3d)
- Similarity threshold: 60% word overlap for legal text grouping
- Confidence cap: Prevents probability scores >1.0 with multiple model agreements

Auth now only stores userId in localStorage

Changes:
- localStorage now ONLY stores userId (not full user object)
- User data is always fetched fresh from MongoDB on app load
- Automatic session hydration from backend API
- Auto-logout on invalid/expired sessions
- Backend is now the single source of truth

Benefits:
- Eliminates sync issues between localStorage and database
- Always shows fresh, up-to-date user data
- Better security (less data in localStorage)
- Fixes refresh/reload data inconsistencies
- Prepares codebase for JWT token implementation

Implementation Details:
- login(): Saves only userData.id to localStorage
- useEffect hydration: Fetches full user from GET /api/auth/user/:userId
- updateUser(): Updates React state only (no localStorage writes)
- logout(): Clears userId and resets state
- Error handling: Auto-logout on failed hydration

body:
Multiple O(n) operations in 60fps game loop causing frame drops on classroom tablets.

## Changes

### Lane partitioning (44.9% improvement)
Pre-partition objects by lane once instead of filtering 16 times per spawn cycle:

```typescript
// Before: filter called 16 times (8 spawns × 2 calls)
for (let i = 0; i < spawnCount; i++) {
  const laneObjects = [...objects, ...created].filter(obj => obj.lane === lane)
}

// After: partition once, O(1) lookups
const left = [], right = []
for (const obj of objects) {
  obj.lane === 'left' ? left.push(obj) : right.push(obj)
}
const laneObjects = lane === 'left' ? [...left, ...createdLeft] : [...right, ...createdRight]
```

### Object updates (54.9% improvement)
- Pre-allocate arrays to eliminate dynamic resizing overhead
- Explicit construction instead of spread operator reduces allocations from 1,800/sec to 720/sec at 60fps

### Event tracking (O(n) → O(1))
Removed forEach loop updating all emoji stats on each appearance. Calculate `timeSinceLastAppearance` on-demand in getters.

### Minor optimizations
- Early exit in duplicate checking (55.7% improvement)
- Hoist viewport lookups out of worm update map function

## Validation

Performance test suite added with benchmarks confirming improvements. Collision detection already optimal (86.7% fewer checks than naive O(n²)).

Bundle impact: +3.7% (15.56 kB) for runtime gains.

body:
## Summary
Fixes the race condition where docs aren't regenerated after provider code regeneration.

## Related Issue
Fixes #357

## Changes Made
- Modified `create-regeneration-pr` job to regenerate docs when EITHER:
  1. The standalone docs job found changes (templates/examples), OR
  2. Provider code was regenerated (schema descriptions may have changed)

## Problem Solved
When `generate-all-schemas.go` is modified to change MarkdownDescription output,
the docs were not being regenerated because:
1. Standalone docs job ran with OLD provider code → "no changes"
2. Provider regeneration created NEW descriptions
3. Docs regeneration was skipped due to step 1's output

Now docs will always regenerate after provider regeneration.

## Testing
This will be tested when the workflow runs on the next merge to main.

author: copilot
body:
Implements production-grade MLOps infrastructure for the face attribute classification pipeline. Adds automated orchestration, continuous integration/deployment, drift detection, and comprehensive monitoring.

## Airflow Orchestration

**3 DAGs for automated ML workflows:**

- `ml_pipeline_dag.py`: Weekly execution (data validation → preprocessing → training → evaluation → drift check → conditional deployment)
- `data_validation_dag.py`: Daily schema/quality/distribution checks
- `model_retraining_dag.py`: Drift-triggered retraining with A/B comparison and automatic rollback

```python
# DAGs use XCom for task communication
def check_drift(**context):
    monitor = EvidentlyMonitor()
    drift_detected = monitor.check_drift_threshold(threshold=0.1)
    context['ti'].xcom_push(key='drift_detected', value=drift_detected)
    return drift_detected

# Conditional deployment based on drift
def deploy_model(**context):
    if context['ti'].xcom_pull(key='drift_detected', task_ids='check_drift'):
        return "retraining_needed"
    return "deployed"
```

## GitHub Actions CI/CD

**5 workflows for automation:**

- `ci.yml`: Lint (flake8, black) + test (pytest) + type-check (mypy) on push/PR
- `cd.yml`: Docker build/push to ghcr.io on tagged releases
- `dvc-pipeline.yml`: Automated DVC repro on master commits
- `model-training.yml`: Manual training with parameterized inputs (epochs, batch_size, learning_rate)
- `monitoring.yml`: Daily drift checks with auto-issue creation on detection

All workflows include explicit `permissions` blocks per security best practices.

## Evidently AI Drift Monitoring

**Comprehensive drift detection system:**

```python
monitor = EvidentlyMonitor(reference_data_path="src/monitoring/reference_data/reference.csv")

# Data drift with chi-square tests for categorical attributes
report = monitor.generate_data_drift_report(current_data)
drift_detected = monitor.check_drift_threshold(threshold=0.1)

# Model performance degradation tracking
tracker = ModelPerformanceTracker()
drift_results = tracker.detect_performance_drift(threshold=0.05, window_size=5)
```

**Monitors:** beard, mustache, glasses (binary), hair_color (5 classes), hair_length (3 classes)

## Prometheus + Grafana Observability

**Metrics exposed at `/metrics` endpoint:**

- API: `api_requests_total`, `api_request_latency_seconds`
- Model: `model_predictions_total`, `model_inference_latency_seconds`, `model_confidence_score`
- Drift: `drift_score{attribute}`, `model_accuracy{attribute}`
- System: `model_loaded`, `cache_size`, `images_processed_total`

**3 pre-configured Grafana dashboards:**

1. ML Metrics: predictions distribution, confidence heatmap, latency P50/P95/P99, drift timeline, per-attribute accuracy
2. API Performance: RPS, latency by endpoint, error rate, status code distribution
3. System Metrics: CPU/memory usage, disk I/O, network traffic, container stats

**Alert rules:** High latency (P95 >500ms), high error rate (>5%), model not loaded, drift detected (>0.2), low accuracy (<0.7)

## Infrastructure

```yaml
# docker-compose.full.yml - complete stack
services:
  - api (ML service)
  - mlflow (experiment tracking)
  - prometheus (metrics)
  - grafana (visualization)
  - alertmanager (alerting)
  - airflow-webserver, airflow-scheduler (orchestration)
  - postgres (Airflow backend)
  - node-exporter, cadvisor (system metrics)
```

**Utility scripts:**

- `scripts/run_drift_check.py`: Standalone drift detection (data, model, Evidently)
- `scripts/export_metrics.py`: Manual Prometheus gauge updates

## Documentation

- `docs/monitoring.md`: Prometheus/Grafana/Evidently setup and configuration
- `docs/airflow.md`: DAG development, custom operators, best practices
- `docs/ci-cd.md`: Workflow configuration, secrets management, deployment strategies
- `monitoring/README.md`: Quick start for monitoring stack
- `README.md`: Complete project overview with usage examples

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

Intégrer les composants MLOps avancés (Airflow, GitHub Actions, Evidently AI, Grafana + Prometheus) dans la branche `devlopment` existante.

- Déploiement API + Docker (FastAPI, frontend web)
- Configuration DVC
- MLflow tracking amélioré

### 07/ Airflow - Orchestration des pipelines ML

Créer la structure suivante :
```
airflow/
├── dags/

- Déclenché par drift détecté
- Réentraîne le modèle automatiquement

### 08/ GitHub Actions - CI/CD complet

.github/

**dvc-pipeline.yml:**

- Run dvc repro
- Push results

**model-training.yml:**

- Inputs: epochs, batch_size, learning_rate
- Entraînement avec MLflow
- Upload model artifact

**monitoring.yml:**
- Trigger: schedule (daily)
- Run Evidently drift check
- Create issue si drift détecté

### 09/ Evidently AI - Monitoring Data/Model Drift

Créer la structure suivante :
```
src/monitoring/
├── __init__.py
├── evidently_monitoring.py         # Classe EvidentlyMonitor
├── data_drift.py                   # Détection drift données

evidently_workspace/                # Workspace Evidently UI

```

**evidently_monitoring.py:**
- Classe `EvidentlyMonitor`:
  - `generate_data_drift_report(current_data)` - Rapport drift données

  - `generate_target_drift_report()` - Drift des prédictions
  - `check_drift_threshold(threshold=0.1)` - Vérification seuil
  - `save_html_report(path)` - Export HTML
  
- Métriques Evidently à utiliser:
  - DataDriftPreset
  - DataQualityPreset

  - ColumnDriftMetric pour chaque attribut

**data_drift.py:**
- Comparaison distribution attributs (beard, mustache, glasses, hair_color, hair_length)
- Détection changements statistiques
- Alertes automatiques

**model_drift.py:**
- Comparaison accuracy/precision/recall au fil du temps
- Détection dégradation performance
- Seuils configurables

author: realmarcin
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive optimization of the D4D schema's ontology grounding based on expert review feedback from Harry Caufield. Reduced from **40+ to 25+ standards** by removing redundant, unused, and overly granular ontology mappings while maintaining essential semantic interoperability.

## Changes Overview

### Phase 1-3: Remove Unused Standards (Commit 4df82e6)
**Removed 7 standards with minimal/unclear benefit:**
- VoID (Vocabulary of Interlinked Datasets)
- W3C Formats Registry (redundant with IANA Media Types)
- FOAF (Friend of a Friend) - replaced with schema.org
- BIBO (Bibliographic Ontology)
- OSLC (Open Services for Lifecycle Collaboration)
- Frictionless Data Standards (initial removal)
- XSD from VariableTypeEnum (kept in schema.org mappings)

**Replaced PAV with Dublin Core:**
- 9 PAV usages → Dublin Core equivalents
- version → dcterms:hasVersion
- previousVersion → dcterms:isVersionOf
- createdOn → dcterms:created
- createdBy → dcterms:creator
- lastUpdateOn → dcterms:modified

**Removed CSVW from Variables module:**
- 6 CSVW usages removed (Column, name, datatype, primaryKey, null, dialect)

### Phase 4: Reduce PROV-O to Essential Use (Commit 4df82e6)
- **Before**: 21 PROV-O mappings across schema
- **After**: 1 essential mapping (was_derived_from slot)
- **Removed**: Agent roles (9 mappings in CreatorOrMaintainerEnum)
- **Rationale**: Redundant with schema.org and Dublin Core

### Phase 5-6: Remove Security Classification Mappings (Commit 4df82e6)
**Removed from ConfidentialityLevelEnum:**
- ISO 27001 mappings (Public, Internal, Highly Confidential)
- NIST SP 800-60 mappings (Low Impact, Moderate Impact, High Impact)
- Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) mappings (TLP:CLEAR, TLP:GREEN, TLP:AMBER)

**Rationale**: Security classification is domain-specific; prescriptive mappings may not fit all use cases

### Phase 9: Remove GDPR and EU AI Act - US-Centric Focus (Commit 4fc1f85)
**Per Harry's feedback: "stay US-centric"**

**Removed from D4D_Data_Governance.yaml:**
- `gdpr_compliant` field from ExportControlRegulatoryRestrictions
- `eu_ai_act_risk_category` field from ExportControlRegulatoryRestrictions
- Entire `AIActRiskEnum` (42 lines):
  - minimal_risk (EUAIAct:Article50)
  - limited_risk (EUAIAct:Article50, EUAIAct:TitleIV)
  - high_risk (EUAIAct:Article6, EUAIAct:AnnexIII, EUAIAct:TitleIII)
  - unacceptable_risk (EUAIAct:Article5)

**Updated descriptions:**
- ComplianceStatusEnum: "GDPR, HIPAA, EU AI Act" → "HIPAA, 45 CFR 46"
- ExportControlRegulatoryRestrictions: Now references "HIPAA and other US regulations"
- D4D_Base_import Composition: Removed GDPR reference
- D4D_Human regulatory_compliance: "(45 CFR 46, GDPR, HIPAA)" → "(45 CFR 46, HIPAA)"

### Phase 10: Complete Frictionless & CSVW Cleanup (Commit 4fc1f85)
**Per Harry's feedback: "wouldn't worry about mapping to it" (Frictionless), "more granular than D4D needs" (CSVW)**

**Prefix removals:**
- `frictionless: https://specs.frictionlessdata.io/` (from D4D_Base_import.yaml and data_sheets_schema.yaml)
- `csvw: http://www.w3.org/ns/csvw#` (from D4D_Base_import.yaml and data_sheets_schema.yaml)

**Mapping removals:**
- `slot_uri: csvw:dialect` from dialect slot in D4D_Base_import.yaml

## Harry Caufield's Feedback Alignment

| Recommendation | Status | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Remove FOAF | ✅ Complete | Phase 1: Replaced with schema.org |
| Remove BIBO | ✅ Complete | Phase 1: Removed (minimal usage) |
| Keep AIO | ✅ Complete | Retained: BiasTypeEnum (9 bias types) |
| Reduce PROV-O | ✅ Complete | Phase 4: 21→1 usages (kept derivation) |
| Keep DUO | ✅ Complete | Retained: DataUsePermissionEnum (22 types) |
| Keep CRediT | ✅ Complete | Retained: CreatorOrMaintainerEnum mappings |
| Remove GDPR | ✅ Complete | Phase 9: Removed gdpr_compliant field |
| Remove EU AI Act | ✅ Complete | Phase 9: Removed AIActRiskEnum entirely |
| Remove Frictionless | ✅ Complete | Phase 10: Removed prefixes |
| Remove CSVW | ✅ Complete | Phase 10: Removed prefixes + mappings |

**Result**: 100% alignment with expert recommendations (10/10 items)

## Impact Analysis

### Standards Count
- **Before**: 40+ standards, ontologies, and frameworks
- **After**: 25+ standards (37.5% reduction)

### Code Changes
**Commit 4df82e6 (Phases 1-8):**
- 15 files changed
- 1,104 insertions(+)
- 1,338 deletions(-)

**Commit 4fc1f85 (Phases 9-10):**
- 10 files changed
- 750 insertions(+)
- 995 deletions(-)

**Total:**
- 25 files changed (with overlap)
- 1,854 insertions(+)
- 2,333 deletions(-)

### Retained Essential Standards

**Ontologies (5):**
1. AIO - Artificial Intelligence Ontology (bias taxonomy)
2. DUO - Data Use Ontology (GA4GH permissions)
3. PROV-O - Provenance (minimal use: derivation only)
4. SKOS - Knowledge organization
5. Biolink - Biomedical knowledge graphs

**Metadata Standards (6):**
1. Dublin Core (dcterms) - Core metadata vocabulary
2. DCAT - Data catalog vocabulary
3. schema.org - Structured data markup
4. DataCite - Dataset citation metadata
5. QUDT - Units and quantities
6. Bridge2AI Standards Registry

**Regulatory Frameworks (US-Centric) (2):**
1. HIPAA - Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
2. 45 CFR 46 - Common Rule for human subjects research

**Attribution Standards (1):**
1. CRediT - Contributor Roles Taxonomy

**Technical Standards (3):**
1. IANA Media Types
2. SPDX Licenses
3. W3C Recommendations (SHACL, basic)

## Files Changed

### Schema Files (7)
- `src/data_sheets_schema/schema/D4D_Data_Governance.yaml`
- `src/data_sheets_schema/schema/D4D_Base_import.yaml`
- `src/data_sheets_schema/schema/D4D_Human.yaml`
- `src/data_sheets_schema/schema/data_sheets_schema.yaml`
- `src/data_sheets_schema/schema/D4D_Maintenance.yaml`
- `src/data_sheets_schema/schema/D4D_Variables.yaml`
- `src/data_sheets_schema/schema/D4D_Composition.yaml`

### Generated Artifacts (4)
- `src/data_sheets_schema/datamodel/data_sheets_schema.py`
- `project/jsonld/data_sheets_schema.jsonld`
- `project/jsonschema/data_sheets_schema.schema.json`
- `project/owl/data_sheets_schema.owl.ttl`

### Documentation (2)
- `docs/standards_alignment.md` (comprehensive changelog added)
- `docs/enum_ontology_grounding_report.md` (phase documentation)

## Validation

All tests pass successfully:

```bash
✅ make test-modules    # All D4D modules validate
✅ make test-schema     # Full merged schema validates
✅ make gen-project     # All artifacts regenerated
✅ make test            # Complete test suite passes
```

**No breaking changes** - all removed fields were optional.

## Benefits

1. **Reduced Complexity**: Fewer external dependencies to track and maintain
2. **Improved Clarity**: Removed redundant/overlapping mappings
3. **US-Centric Focus**: Aligned with primary user base regulations
4. **Better Maintainability**: Focused on high-impact, well-maintained standards
5. **Expert-Validated**: 100% alignment with expert review feedback

## Documentation

Comprehensive documentation added in commit 4df82e6:
- `docs/standards_alignment.md` - Full standards inventory and rationale
- `docs/enum_ontology_grounding_report.md` - Enumeration ontology analysis
- Both documents include detailed Phase 1-11 changelogs

## Related Issues

Implements recommendations from expert review discussion regarding ontology grounding optimization and standards alignment strategy.

**Steps to reproduce:**
- Install l10n_ar
- Switch to a Argentinian company (e.g. (AR) Responsable Inscripto)
- In Accounting settings, enable "Taxes in company currency" option
- Activate another currency (e.g. USD)

- Create an invoice in USD
- Confirm the invoice
- Print the invoice

**Issue:**
The section showing the taxes in the company currency doesn't appear on the invoice despite the enabled option.

Cause:
An override of "report_invoice_document" from l10n_are is removing the section no matter what the configuration.

**Solution:**
Do not remove the section.
It was done originally in 17.0 where "Taxes in company currency" option didn't exist.

author: autumnsgrove
body:
The @autumnsgrove/groveengine package wasn't working properly at
Cloudflare Pages runtime because the package lacks a dist folder.
Vite aliases were configured to redirect imports to local files,
but this only worked at build time, not SSR runtime.

This fix replaces all GroveEngine imports in admin routes with
direct $lib imports:
- @autumnsgrove/groveengine/components/ui → $lib/components/ui
- @autumnsgrove/groveengine/utils/api → $lib/utils/api
- @autumnsgrove/groveengine/utils/markdown → $lib/utils/markdown
- @autumnsgrove/groveengine → individual component imports

This should resolve the 500 errors on /admin after authentication.

author: snakewizardd
body:
Implements complete iris dataset transformation and sonification:

Backend:
- R script (iris_transform.R) transforms Fisher's 1936 iris dataset into sinusoidal waves
- Normalizes 4 numeric features to [0,1] range
- Generates composite waves using harmonics at frequencies 1,2,3,4 with phase offsets
- FastAPI router (/api/iris/data) executes R script and returns JSON data
- Health endpoint for iris transformation system

Frontend:
- IrisSonifier class with 4 voices (sepal length/width, petal length/width)
- Different musical scales per species: setosa (major), versicolor (minor), virginica (lydian)
- Effects chain: chorus -> delay -> reverb -> compressor
- Canvas visualization showing sinusoidal waves colored by species
- Interactive species filtering
- Play/stop controls for audio sonification
- Educational information about Fisher's 1936 paper

Navigation:
- Added Iris Sonification link to main page

This feature demonstrates the confluence thesis: where statistics meets soul, where data becomes music, where Fisher's botanical measurements become living sound.

author: 0xthrpw
body:
Summary of Staged Changes (RC6)

  94 files changed, ~14,278 additions, ~369 deletions

  1. Validation System (Major Feature)

  New listing/offer validation infrastructure to detect unfunded listings and offers:

  - Database migrations: 0270_add_validation_tracking.sql - adds last_validated_at, unfunded_at, unfunded_reason columns to listings/offers, plus new validation_state table
  - Workers:
    - validation.ts - core validation logic
    - validate-listing-ownership.ts - verifies sellers still own ENS names
    - validate-offer-balance.ts - checks buyer ETH/WETH/USDC balances
    - batch-validate-offers.ts - bulk offer validation
    - status-update-handler.ts - handles status transitions
    - bootstrap-validation.ts - initial validation seeding script
  - PRD doc: BALANCE_AND_OWNERSHIP_CHECKS.md (1401 lines)

  2. Redis Caching Layer

  - New services/api/src/utils/redis.ts utility
  - New services/api/src/middleware/cache.ts middleware
  - Documentation: REDIS_CACHE.md

  3. POAP System

  - New route: services/api/src/routes/poap.ts
  - Migration: 0290_create_poap_system.sql - poap_links table
  - Script: import-poap-links.ts

  4. Activity History Improvements

  - Split cancelled event type into listing_cancelled and offer_cancelled (migration 0280)
  - Activity notifier enhancements
  - Frontend updates to ActivityHistory.tsx and ProfileActivity.tsx
  - Backfill plan doc: ACTIVITY_HISTORY_BACKFILL_PLAN.md

  5. Mutelist Feature

  - New mutelist table (migration 0310)
  - New service: services/api/src/services/mutelist.ts
  - Filters addresses from WebSocket activity broadcasts

  6. Notification Preferences

  - Migration 0300: adds notify_on_offer_received, notify_on_listing_sold to users
  - Enhanced notifications.ts worker
  - Email service updates

  7. Data Integrity Scripts (wal-listener)

  ~25 new maintenance/fix scripts including:
  - fix-duplicate-names.ts, fix-owner-addresses.ts, fix-token-ids.ts
  - recover-hash-placeholders.ts, recover-null-expiry-dates.ts
  - backfill-mint-events.ts, backfill-registration-dates.ts
  - Various Elasticsearch sync scripts (resync-*, recreate-es-index.ts)

  8. Indexer Enhancements

  - Significant updates to ens-indexer.ts (~329 lines changed)
  - OpenSea stream improvements
  - ENS resolver enhancements
  - New update-ens-names.ts script

  9. API Route Updates

  Minor updates across: activity.ts, clubs.ts, listings.ts, names.ts, offers.ts, sales.ts, search.ts, users.ts, websocket.ts

  10. pg_notify Payload Fix

  Migration 0320: rewrites notify_changes() function to exclude large JSONB fields (order_data, metadata) to stay under the 8000-byte limit

Adds Ollama integration to enable local LLM-powered AI assistant responses instead of mock data.

## Changes

### New: `src/lib/ollama.ts`
- API client for Ollama server with connection status, model listing, chat/generate endpoints
- Streaming support via async generator
- Timeout handling using `AbortController` (not `AbortSignal.timeout()` for compatibility)

### Modified: `src/components/ai-assistant/AIAssistant.tsx`
- Connection status indicator with manual refresh
- Model selector dropdown populated from Ollama `/api/tags`
- Toggle to switch between Ollama and mock responses
- Graceful fallback when Ollama unavailable

## Usage

```typescript
import { getOllamaClient } from '@/lib/ollama';

const client = getOllamaClient();
const status = await client.checkConnection();  // { connected: true, version: "0.1.x" }
const models = await client.listModels();        // [{ name: "llama3:8b", size: 4.7GB, ... }]
const response = await client.chat([
  { role: 'user', content: '查看钱包余额' }
]);
```

Requires Ollama running locally (`ollama serve`) with at least one model pulled.

This pull request updates the `.github/workflows/python-publish.yml` workflow to introduce automated testing for multiple Python versions and ensure that the release build only runs after successful tests. The main changes are grouped below:

**Continuous Integration improvements:**

* Added a `test` job that runs on Ubuntu and tests the codebase against Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 using `pytest`. This job installs dependencies (`pytest`, `polars`, `pyarrow`) and runs tests for each Python version in the matrix.

**Release process enhancements:**

* Updated the `release-build` job to depend on the `test` job, ensuring that releases only happen after tests pass. Also added an output for the `package_version` from the `get_version` step

author: kontramind
body:
This commit implements Phase 1 of the OpenDataVal integration:

Dependencies:
- Changed requires-python from >=3.12 to >=3.11,<3.13 (OpenDataVal/PyTorch doesn't support Python 3.12+ yet)
- Added opendataval>=1.0.0,<2.0.0 as optional dependency

Core Implementation (sdvaluation/valuator.py):
- Add 'backend' parameter to LGBMDataValuator class
  - Supports "custom" (default) and "opendataval" backends
  - Custom backend: existing TMCS with uncertainty quantification
  - OpenDataVal backend: library-based implementation (no CI in Phase 1)
- Refactor compute_shapley_values() to dispatch between backends
  - Renamed original implementation to _compute_shapley_custom()
  - Added new _compute_shapley_opendataval() method
- Update save_results() to handle missing CI metrics gracefully

Workflow Integration:
- Add --backend CLI flag with default="custom" (sdvaluation/cli.py)
- Update run_data_valuation() to pass backend parameter (sdvaluation/core.py)
- Add documentation and examples for both backends

Features:
- Backwards compatible: default behavior unchanged
- Clean architecture for future expansion (Phase 2 & 3)
- Proper error handling and validation
- Works with Python 3.11

Installation:
- Default: uv sync (custom backend only)
- With OpenDataVal: uv sync --extra opendataval

Note: Phase 1 does not include confidence intervals for opendataval backend. Future phases will add convergence-based CI and additional model support.

body:
This PR uses `WorkloadAttestorsVerification` API to configure how the SPIRE agent verifies kubelet certificates. 
It supports `skip`, `auto`, and `hostCert` modes with conditional hostPath mounting for custom CA certificates:
1. `skip`: Skips kubelet TLS certificate verification entirely
2. `hostCert`: Uses a custom CA certificate from the host filesystem. Requires both `hostCertBasePath` and `hostCertFileName` (enforced via CEL validation)
3. `auto`: Enables kubelet verification. If custom paths are specified, uses them. Otherwise, SPIRE uses its default cluster CA bundle (`/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt`).

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR addresses the deadlock issues observed in Direct Mode benchmarks. 

Key changes include:
1.  **Memory Layout Alignment:** Added explicit padding to `SlotHeader` in both C++ and Go to ensuring correct memory alignment and prevent false sharing between cache lines.
2.  **Robust Synchronization:** Enhanced the Go worker loop to use a timeout-based `WaitForEvent` loop, preventing infinite hangs if a signal is missed or spurious wakeup occurs.
3.  **Correct Memory Ordering:** Upgraded memory orderings in C++ `DirectHost` to `seq_cst` for critical state flags to ensure visibility across threads/processes.
4.  **Safe Defaults:** Hardcoded the default polling target to 1 in Go to prevent CPU starvation in constrained container environments.
5.  **Cleanup:** Added `.gitignore` to exclude benchmark logs and binaries.

body:
Redesigns the Trade Finder with an interactive three-panel interface for building trades, incorporating park-adjusted player ratings and multiple trade matching modes (Fair Trade, Buy Low, Fleece Mode).

## Park-Adjusted Player Ratings

- **Batters**: Adjusts power (PF HR) and contact (PF AVG) scores. Players in pitcher-friendly parks get boosted adjusted ratings.
- **Pitchers**: Inverse logic—pitchers in hitter-friendly parks get boosted ratings.

```python
# Batter in Oracle Park (PF HR=0.85)
result = calculate_park_adjusted_batter_score(player, team_data)
# power_raw: 60.0 → power_adjusted: 70.6 (boosted for suppressive park)
```

## Trade Builder Tab (`gui/trade_builder_tab.py`)

- **Left Panel**: Team selector + player list with checkboxes, surplus value, park-adjusted ratings
- **Right Panel**: Filters (position, age, team status) + trade mode toggle + search results
- **Bottom Panel**: Side-by-side comparison, trade grade (A+ to F), park impact preview

## Trade Value Calculation

```python
trade_value = (
    base_surplus_value        # WAR × $8M/WAR - salary
    + park_adjustment_bonus   # Value boost for suppressive park
    + age_adjustment          # Young players worth more
    + contract_value          # Years of control, salary efficiency
)
```

## Trade Modes

| Mode | Tolerance | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| ⚖️ Fair Trade | ±10% | Equal value matches |
| 📈 Buy Low | ±25% | Prioritizes undervalued players, surfaces hidden gems |
| 🎰 Fleece Mode | +50% | Returns lopsided trades (for fun) |

## Hidden Gems Integration

Buy Low mode surfaces park-suppressed hidden gems automatically:
- Batter in extreme pitcher park (PF < 0.95 or PF HR < 0.90) with good raw power/contact
- Pitcher in extreme hitter park (PF > 1.05 or PF HR > 1.10) with good raw stuff
- On seller team with good surplus value

## Files Changed

- `batters.py` — `calculate_park_adjusted_batter_score()`, `get_park_impact_preview()`
- `pitchers.py` — `calculate_park_adjusted_pitcher_score()`, `get_pitcher_park_impact_preview()`
- `team_parser.py` — `calculate_comprehensive_trade_value()`, `calculate_trade_grade()`, `find_hidden_gem_trade_targets()`
- `gui/trade_builder_tab.py` — New tab implementation
- `gui/core.py` — Tab integration
- `README.md` — Documentation

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Overview

Redesign the Trade Finder tab with an interactive interface for building and evaluating trades, incorporating park-adjusted player ratings and multiple trade matching modes.

## Part 1: Park-Adjusted Player Ratings

Add park factor adjustments to player evaluation by matching players to their team's park factors via the `ORG` field (player) → `Abbr` field (team).

### For Batters:
- Adjust power scores using `PF HR` from team data
- Adjust contact/batting scores using `PF AVG`
- Formula concept: `adjusted_score = raw_score * (1 / park_factor)` for hitters (lower park factor = higher adjusted score)
- Store both "raw" and "park-adjusted" ratings

### For Pitchers:
- Inverse logic - pitchers in hitter-friendly parks get boosted ratings
- Adjust using overall `PF` factor
- Formula concept: `adjusted_score = raw_score * park_factor` for pitchers

---

## Part 2: Redesigned Trade Interface

Replace the current static Trade Finder with an interactive three-panel layout.

### Left Panel: "Your Trade Assets"
- **Team Selector Dropdown** at top - populated from loaded team data
- **Player List** showing all players from selected team:
  - Columns: Name, POS, Age, OVR, Salary, Years Left, Surplus Value, Park-Adj Rating
  - **Checkboxes** to select players to trade away
- **Running Total** at bottom showing combined "Trade Value Offered"

### Right Panel: "Trade Targets / Search Results"
- **Filter Controls:**
  - Position filter (checkboxes like existing tabs)
  - Age range (min/max spinboxes or sliders)
  - Salary range (min/max)
  - Team Status filter: Buyers / Sellers / Neutral / All
  - OVR/WAR minimum
- **Trade Mode Toggle** (radio buttons or dropdown):
  - ⚖️ **Fair Trade** - Returns players of equal value (±10% tolerance)
  - 📈 **Buy Low** - Prioritizes undervalued players (seller teams, park-suppressed stats, good surplus value)
  - 🎰 **Fleece Mode** - Simulates bad GM trades; returns players where you get significantly more value than you give (for fun/what-if scenarios)
- **Results List** showing matching players with:
  - Name, POS, Team, Age, OVR, Salary, Surplus Value
  - Value comparison indicator vs. your offered package
  - Checkboxes to select players to receive

### Bottom Panel: "Trade Summary"
- **Side-by-side comparison:**
  - Left: Players you're trading away (names, combined value)
  - Right: Players you're receiving (names, combined value)
- **Trade Grade**: A+ to F based on value differential
  - A+: You gain 30%+ value
  - A: You gain 15-30%
  - B: Roughly fair (±15%)
  - C: You lose 15-30%
  - D: You lose 30-50%
  - F: You lose 50%+ (fleeced!)
- **Park Factor Impact Preview**: Show projected stat changes for players moving parks
  - Example: "Player X: +5 HR projection in new park (Oracle → Citizens Bank)"

---

The "Buy Low" trade mode should surface hidden gems automatically:

### Hidden Gem Criteria:
- Plays in extreme pitcher park (PF < 0.95 or PF HR < 0.90)
- Has good raw power/contact skills being suppressed
- On a seller team (more likely available via trade)
- Good surplus value (underpaid relative to production)

### Display:
- Add a "💎 Hidden Gem" badge/indicator on qualifying players
- Sort/prioritize these in Buy Low mode
- Show "Park-Adjusted Upside" - the gap between current and projected neutral-park stats

Enhance the existing surplus value calculation to create a comprehensive trade value:

```python
trade_value = (
    base_surplus_value           # WAR-based, from existing calculation
    + park_adjustment_bonus      # Value added if in suppressive park
    + age_adjustment             # Young players worth more

- Clear visual separation between the three panels

body:
## Overview

This PR updates the MLC course materials to be compatible with TVM latest API changes. This is the first step in modernizing the course content, focusing on API updates. Additional content updates will follow in subsequent PRs.

## Changes

### API Updates

1. **Compilation API**
   - `tvm.build()` → `tvm.compile()` for TIR modules
   - `relax.build()` → `tvm.compile()` for Relax modules
   - `lib.time_evaluator()` → `lib.mod.time_evaluator()` (tvm.compile returns Executable with mod attribute)

2. **Runtime API**
   - `tvm.nd.array()` → `tvm.runtime.tensor()`
   - `tvm.nd.empty()` → `tvm.runtime.tensor(np.empty(...))`
   - Type annotations: `tvm.nd.NDArray` → `tvm.runtime.Tensor`

3. **Function Registration**
   - `@tvm.register_func()` → `@tvm.register_global_func()`

### Code Fixes

- Fixed syntax errors in code blocks
- Updated installation commands (`mlc-ai-nightly` → `mlc-ai-nightly-cpu`)
- Fixed pseudo-code syntax issues

## Next Steps

In the following PR, I will update repo `mlc-zn`  as well and then include updating outdated usage
(like `PyTorch FX`->`exported_program`).

# Augment "Compare Offers" Page 
Note: branched off of [Jack's open PR](https://github.com/inisperos/sunny-savings/pull/8) since this will be merged. Seeks to avoid merge conflicts. 

## Purpose
This PR responds to Yijun's feedback about how only being able to compare 2 internship offers was too restrictive. Earlier user research indicated this was also the case. Functionality has been added to compare up to 4 offers at a time. 

## Key Changes 
**All changes made in `ComparePlansPage.jsx`** 
1. Define global `const MAX_PLANS`. Currently set to four, could be changed later (this would likely require minor changes in styling of containers)  
2. Establishes `planMap` to map offers to list index in the order they are selected by the user 
3. Updated the selection logic (`toggle` function) to allow up to `MAX_PLANS` to be selected in the checkbox UI.
4. Refactored the main comparison area from a single horizontal grid into a two-row vertical grid layout
a. Row 1 (Chart): Contains the `MidChart` component, which now spans the full width.
b. Row 2 (Summaries): Contains an inner grid that dynamically creates columns for each selected offer summary.

## Summary

- Implements direct storage API access for the Payment transaction, bypassing SQL parsing overhead
- Uses the same pattern as New-Order and Delivery transactions for consistency
- Payment now uses PK lookups for warehouse/district/customer (by ID) and index scan for customer-by-name queries

## Performance Results

**Payment-only benchmark (SF=1, 5s):**
| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Avg latency | 15.89 µs | 0.63 µs | **25x faster** |
| Throughput | 60,623 TPS | 747,038 TPS | **12x higher** |

**Comparison with other databases:**
| Database | TPS | Avg (µs) |
|----------|-----|----------|
| VibeSQL | 747,038 | 0.63 |
| SQLite | 111,775 | 8.39 |
| DuckDB | 845 | 1,183 |

VibeSQL is now **6.7x faster than SQLite** for Payment transactions.

## Test plan

- [x] TPC-C Payment benchmark verifies correctness (100% success rate)
- [x] TPC-C mixed workload completes successfully  
- [x] `cargo test --release -p vibesql-executor` passes

Closes #3371

author: frankbria
body:
## Problem

E2E backend and frontend tests were consistently failing in GitHub Actions with timeout errors:
```
Error: Timed out waiting for: http://localhost:8080/health
```

**Root Cause**: `uv run uvicorn` triggers a package rebuild on every invocation, adding 20-30 seconds to startup time. Combined with the 60-second timeout, the server couldn't start in time.

## Solution

This PR implements comprehensive fixes to resolve the timeout issues:

### Backend E2E Tests
- ✅ Pre-install package with `uv pip install -e .` (eliminates rebuild overhead)
- ✅ Initialize database explicitly before server startup
- ✅ Use direct venv Python invocation instead of `uv run`
- ✅ Increase timeout from 60s → 120s
- ✅ Add retry loop with progress feedback (120 attempts @ 1s)
- ✅ Verify server process health after 5s
- ✅ Capture server logs for debugging
- ✅ Upload logs as artifacts (7-day retention)

### Frontend E2E Tests
- ✅ Apply same backend server improvements
- ✅ Sequential server startup (backend → frontend)
- ✅ Separate health checks (120s backend, 60s frontend)
- ✅ Capture both backend and frontend logs
- ✅ Better error messages showing which server failed

### Environment Configuration
- Set `DATABASE_PATH` to `${{ github.workspace }}/.codeframe/state.db`
- Set `WORKSPACE_ROOT` to `${{ github.workspace }}`
- Set `CODEFRAME_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=self_hosted`

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/test.yml`**: Updated E2E test jobs with timeout fixes
- **`E2E_TESTS_FIX_PLAN.md`**: Full implementation plan and documentation

## Expected Impact

- 📉 Reduces server startup time by 20-30 seconds
- ⏱️ Provides 120-second total timeout (was 60s)
- 🔍 Better diagnostics with server logs on failure
- 🚨 Immediate crash detection before timeout
- 📝 Clearer error messages and progress feedback

## Testing

- [x] Local server startup confirmed working (<5s after package install)
- [x] Health endpoint confirmed functional (`/health` returns JSON)
- [ ] Will validate in CI on this PR

## Success Criteria

- ✅ E2E backend tests complete within 3 minutes
- ✅ E2E frontend tests complete within 5 minutes
- ✅ Server starts within 30 seconds
- ✅ Health endpoint responds successfully
- ✅ Logs available for debugging on failure

## Related Issues

Closes timeout issues in E2E tests reported in recent CI runs.

## Checklist

- [x] Implementation complete
- [x] Documentation added (E2E_TESTS_FIX_PLAN.md)
- [x] Changes tested locally
- [ ] CI tests pass (will verify in this PR)

author: srskyflow
body:
This pull request updates the `OfferProvider` component in `OfferContext.jsx` to improve how offer data is refreshed and how loading indicators are managed. The main changes introduce periodic background refreshing of offers without disrupting the user experience and refine loading state handling.

**Offer data refresh improvements:**

* Added a polling mechanism using `setInterval` in the `useEffect` hook to refresh offer data every 3 seconds in the background, preventing unnecessary loading indicators during silent updates.

**Loading state management:**

* Updated the `fetchOffers` function to accept a `silent` parameter, so that loading indicators are only shown for non-silent fetches. This prevents UI flicker during background refreshes.
* Modified the logic in both the start and end of `fetchOffers` to conditionally set the loading state based on the `silent` flag. author: danval-003
body:
This pull request introduces several changes across documentation, authentication logic, and UI components. The most significant update is the addition of a comprehensive Spanish-language project overview and setup guide, which improves onboarding and understanding for new contributors. There are also enhancements to device information capture during authentication, minor UI adjustments for better visual consistency, and a new polyfill to ensure compatibility with certain runtime environments.

**Documentation and onboarding improvements:**

* Added a detailed Spanish-language project overview and setup guide in `adsasd.md`, including methodology, results, usage instructions, dataset details, and citation information. This greatly improves onboarding and context for new contributors.

**Authentication and device integration:**

* In `src/auth/useAuth.ts`, device information is now captured using `expo-device` and sent with login requests, enabling improved tracking and auditing of authentication events. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-550f7ef0b79de9a0b1d6c90faed36fb3863a093e264f6b18cb6e44748f37df56R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-550f7ef0b79de9a0b1d6c90faed36fb3863a093e264f6b18cb6e44748f37df56L18-R29)

**UI consistency and usability:**

* Changed the text size for help messages in `Label` components from `sm` to `xs` for a more compact display.
* Updated the `DatasetSelect` component to use a smaller text size (`sm` instead of `md`) for header labels, enhancing visual hierarchy.

**Runtime compatibility:**

* Added a polyfill in `polyfills.ts` to ensure Hermes exposes the `_toString` helper, improving compatibility with dependencies that expect JSC globals.

**Cleanup:**

* Removed the unused `gen_secrets.py` script, reducing clutter in the codebase.

This commit introduces the complete, deterministic simulation executive for the PSTAS architecture, compliant with the PSTAS-CAT Formal Model.

Key features include:
- An `APSTASimulator` actor that runs a deterministic, multi-task simulation on BeginPlay, with its tick disabled.
- A `pstast_core_config.h` header that defines the mandatory PNDF safety check (`run_pndf_check`) and the core `TAV_THRESHOLD` constant.
- A simulation executive that executes a suite of predefined tasks, including nominal cases and deliberate failure cases to verify the PNDF logic for WCET overruns, TAV underruns, and compound failures.
- A detailed JSON logging system that produces a final report summarizing the results of all tasks, including a stage-by-stage breakdown of the nominal WCET budget for verification.

This implementation has been iteratively refined through multiple code reviews to ensure it is correct, complete, and fully compliant with all directives.

## Summary

This PR implements WASM performance optimizations that reduce document conversion time by approximately **50-55%**.

### Key Changes

- **Pre-indexed style lookups**: Build dictionary indexes once at formatting assembly start, replacing O(n) linear searches with O(1) lookups
- **Paragraph style rollup caching**: Cache rolled-up paragraph properties by style name for non-list-item paragraphs
- **Code cleanup**: Removal of unused virtualization code and session API
- **Profiling infrastructure**: Added profiling harness and documentation

### Performance Results

Tested on HC007-Test-02.docx (210 paragraphs, 8 tables):

| Operation | Before | After | Improvement |
|-----------|--------|-------|-------------|
| GetDocumentMetadata | 617ms | 278ms | **55% faster** |
| ConvertDocxToHtml | 2.37s | 1.15s | **51% faster** |
| ConvertDocxToHtmlWithPagination | 1.65s | 752ms | **54% faster** |
| ConvertDocxToHtmlComplete | 1.49s | 667ms | **55% faster** |

### Files Changed

- `Docxodus/FormattingAssembler.cs` - Style indexing and caching optimizations
- `Docxodus/WmlToHtmlConverter.cs` - Removed unused page range code
- `wasm/DocxodusWasm/DocumentConverter.cs` - Simplified API
- `npm/src/*` - Removed virtualization and session types
- `docs/architecture/wasm-optimization-plan.md` - Optimization documentation

## Test plan

- [x] All 1067 .NET tests pass
- [x] All profiling tests pass
- [x] WASM build succeeds
- [x] Performance improvement verified via profiling harness
