author: jantvrdik
body:
## Summary

Initial implementation of the PHPUnit Parallel Job Balancer library, based on the internal ShipMonk implementation.

This CLI tool balances PHPUnit test execution across parallel jobs based on historical timing data from JUnit XML reports, helping optimize CI pipeline execution time.

### Features
- Parses JUnit XML reports for test timing data
- Uses greedy bin-packing algorithm with tree splitting for optimal distribution
- Generates PHPUnit-compatible testsuite XML fragments
- Configurable job count, exclusions, and output options

### CLI Options
- `--jobs/-j`: Number of parallel jobs (default: 16)
- `--exclude/-e`: Paths to exclude from output (repeatable)
- `--output/-o`: Output file (default: stdout)
- `--tests-dir`: Base test directory (default: ./tests)

### Key Changes from Internal Implementation
- Generalized all hardcoded values (job count, exclusions, tests directory)
- Removed internal ShipMonk dependencies (BaseCommand, Cast, Team, LogicException)
- Replaced Nette Utils with native PHP implementations
- Added Symfony Console for CLI handling
- Full test coverage with 33 tests
- Complete QA setup (PHPStan level max, PHP CodeSniffer, CI workflows)

author: vesker
body:
`Buffer` type is not defined in browser environments, and instead is resolved to `any`. This caused the conditional type `CompactedValue` to resolve `any` type to `string` apart from LiveObject types. One possible way to fix this is to use `ArrayBufferView` in the conditional type instead - it will cover Node's `Buffer` because `Buffer` extends `Uint8Array`, which is an `ArrayBufferView`. And `ArrayBufferView` is a JavaScript type so it works in both environments.

Resolves [AIT-45](https://ably.atlassian.net/browse/AIT-45)

author: krsnapaudel
body:
## Description

Implements the OL mempool for storing pending transactions before block inclusion. Follows a worker-handle pattern with async service framework integration. In some parts, it is inspired by Reth's mempool design.

Updated based on [this design doc](https://www.notion.so/Strata-OL-Mempool-2af901ba000f80fd81a3cbbdb1d850a2?source=copy_link).

### Architecture

**Service Pattern**
- Worker-handle pattern: Internal `MempoolService` runs as async task, external code interacts via `MempoolHandle`
- Two-layer persistence: In-memory `HashMap<OLTxId, MempoolEntry>` for fast access + Sled database backup for crash recovery
- Service framework: Integrates with strata-service for consistent lifecycle management

**Transaction Ordering**
`SnarkAccountUpdate`: Ordered by sequence number (`seq_no`), with `insertion_id` as tiebreaker
`GenericAccountMessage`: FIFO using `first_seen_slot`, with `insertion_id` as tiebreaker

**Per-Account Tracking**
- `account_state`: HashMap<AccountId, AccountMempoolState>` index for efficient per-account operations (including txids and seqnos)

### Validation & State Integration

**`StateAccessor` Integration** 
- Fetches `OLState` from storage for current chain tip
- Per-tip caching: State accessor cached and invalidated on chain updates
- Async API: `get_toplevel_ol_state_async()` via storage manager

**Validation Rules** 
Sequence number validation: `tx.seq_no == account.current_seq_no` (basic validation)
Transaction replacement and gap rejection: `tx.seq_no` must be in the range [`min_seq_no`, `max_seq_no +1`] for account
- **Slot bounds**: Validates `min_slot` and `max_slot` constraints
- **Account existence**: Verifies target account exists in state
- **Account type matching**: `SnarkAccountUpdate` must target Snark account

### Chain Updates & Reorg Handling

**Chain Update Processing**
- `chain_update(new_tip)` handles FCM notifications
- Removes expired txs (`max_slot <= current_slot`)
- Invalidates state accessor cache on tip changes
- Revalidates all transactions

This PR was created with help from Claude Code and Cursor AI.

### Type of Change

<!--
Select the type of change your PR introduces (put an `x` in all that apply):
-->

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature/Enhancement (non-breaking change which adds functionality or enhances an existing one)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] New or updated tests
- [ ] Dependency Update

## Notes to Reviewers

Now not handling reorg for chain update.
Also remove the idea of best transactions iterator and marking invalid.
We are only doing `seq_no` checks (by account) using `OLState` and `AccountMempoolState` (tracks txids and seqnos).

I also had to make the snark state seqno mean next expected to avoid replay possiblities with seqno 0.

The diff looks quite scary, but Claude says ~50% is for testing.

The decision to separate block assembly or keep it inside mempool can be deferred to block assembly PR.

Implements foundational architecture for POS (Caisse) module per project requirements. Phase 1 establishes structure and skeleton screens; business logic deferred to Phase 2.

## Architecture

**New module:** `lib/src/screens/admin/pos/`
- `pos_screen.dart` - Main screen with responsive 3-column layout (Products | Cart | Actions)
- `pos_shell_scaffold.dart` - Reusable scaffold for POS screens
- `pos_routes.dart` - Route helpers referencing centralized `AppRoutes.pos`

Layout breakpoint at 800px: 3-column grid (flex 2:1 + 280px fixed) on desktop/tablet, stacked on mobile. All columns display placeholder UI.

## Integration

**Routing:** Added `/pos` route in `main.dart` with admin-only protection via `authProvider`, auto-redirect for non-admin users.

**Module system:** Updated `ModuleId.staffTablet` label to "Caisse / Staff Tablet" in `module_matrix.dart` and `module_id.dart`. Default route now `/pos`.

**Access:** Temporary button in Admin Studio (marked `TODO(POS_PHASE2)` for removal).

## Example

```dart
class PosScreen extends ConsumerStatefulWidget {
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return PosShellScaffold(
      title: 'Caisse',
      child: LayoutBuilder(
        builder: (context, constraints) {
          final isWideScreen = constraints.maxWidth > 800;
          return isWideScreen 
            ? _buildThreeColumnLayout(context, colorScheme)
            : _buildMobileLayout(context, colorScheme);
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

6 unit tests covering widget rendering, layout responsiveness, and route constant consistency.

**No regressions:** Client screens, Builder B3, SuperAdmin, existing staff tablet, and navigation unchanged.

Tu travailles dans un projet Flutter existant, type pizza / resto :

App client + Admin + SuperAdmin + Builder B3.

White-label en place :

RestaurantPlanUnified (plan modules par resto)

module_matrix.dart + module_runtime_mapping.dart

navbar_module_adapter.dart + white_label_route_guard.dart

Les modules sont identifiés via une enum ModuleId (dans module_registry / module_matrix).

Le module Staff Tablet sera notre module CAISSE (POS).

Ne touche pas au Builder B3, au SuperAdmin ni au client existant, sauf indications explicites.

🎯 Objectif global de la phase :
Mettre en place l’architecture du module CAISSE (POS) : routes, fichiers, écrans squelette, sans logique métier avancée.
On prépare le terrain pour les phases suivantes (UI produits, panier, paiements, sync cuisine, etc.).

✅ RÈGLES GÉNÉRALES

Pas de refacto massif, pas de renommage global.

Aucune dépendance supplémentaire dans pubspec.yaml.

Pas de suppression de code existant, juste ajout / petit câblage.

Respecte les patterns déjà utilisés pour les autres écrans admin / studio.

1️⃣ MODULE ID & MATRICE

Vérifie l’enum ModuleId et réutilise le module existant prévu pour la caisse :

Utiliser ModuleId.staff_tablet comme module “Caisse / Staff Tablet”.

Si déjà présent dans module_matrix.dart, laisse les métadonnées comme elles sont pour l’instant (on complétera plus tard).

Si tu dois ajouter une description / label lisible, utilise un label du style :

displayName: "Caisse / Staff tablet"

⚠️ Pour cette phase, ne change pas les règles de filtrage de la navbar ou de route guard.
On fera l’intégration complète module → accès plus tard.

2️⃣ STRUCTURE FICHIERS MODULE CAISSE

Crée un nouveau mini-module pour la caisse, dans une zone claire, par exemple :

lib/src/screens/pos/ ou lib/src/screens/admin/pos/

Dedans, crée au minimum ces fichiers :

pos_screen.dart

Écran principal de la caisse (POS).

pos_shell_scaffold.dart

Scaffold réutilisable spécifique POS (app bar, body, etc.).

pos_routes.dart (ou intégré dans un fichier pos_module.dart)

Centralise les constantes de route + helpers.

⚠️ Si la structure actuelle du projet impose un autre chemin plus logique (ex : lib/src/screens/admin/staff_tablet/...), aligne-toi dessus, mais reste cohérent.

3️⃣ ROUTES GO_ROUTER – POS

Utilise le système de routing existant (go_router).

Ajoute une route pour l’écran caisse :

Exemple : /pos ou /staff-tablet (choisis un nom clair, cohérent projet).

Route de type admin / staff (pas visible côté client classique).

Intègre cette route dans main.dart là où sont déclarées les autres routes admin :

On veut pouvoir y accéder par URL directe (ex : go('/pos')).

N’ajoute pas de nouvel onglet dans la bottom-nav client pour l’instant.

La caisse sera plutôt accessible via admin (plus tard : bouton spécifique dans l’admin).

🔐 Si le projet utilise déjà un guard d’auth / admin, applique-le aussi sur la route POS :

Accessible uniquement aux admins / staff autorisés (pas aux utilisateurs anonymes).

4️⃣ UI : POS_SCREEN (SQUELETTE UNIQUEMENT)

Dans pos_screen.dart, implémente :

Un StatefulWidget ou ConsumerStatefulWidget (si Riverpod déjà utilisé côté admin).

Utilise un scaffold spécifique (via PosShellScaffold) qui contient :

AppBar avec titre : "Caisse" (et éventuellement sous-titre resto/restaurantId si tu peux le lire facilement).

Body en layout 3 colonnes placeholder :

[ Col 1 : Catégories / Produits (placeholder) ]
[ Col 2 : Panier (placeholder) ]
[ Col 3 : Actions (paiement, infos client, etc.) (placeholder) ]


Sur mobile : layout en colonne ou avec LayoutBuilder/OrientationBuilder pour éviter de casser l’existant.

Mets des Container / Card avec juste :

Un titre "Produits (à implémenter)",

"Panier (à implémenter)",

"Actions caisse (à implémenter)".

Pas de logique métier, pas de Firestore, pas de personnalisation, juste la structure visible.

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new `monthHeaderPosition` prop that allows developers to control the placement of the month header within the calendar. The header can now be positioned at the top (default), middle (between day names and calendar days), or bottom of the calendar.

## Motivation

Provides greater flexibility for calendar layout customization, enabling developers to create more diverse calendar designs while maintaining all existing functionality.

## Changes

### Component Updates
- **DatePicker**: Added `monthHeaderPosition` prop and passed it to `PopperComponent`
- **PopperComponent**: Accepts `monthHeaderPosition` and applies corresponding CSS classes
- **Calendar**: Implements conditional rendering logic for three header positions
- **Month**: Added `monthHeader` and `monthFooter` props for content injection

### Styling
- Added `.react-datepicker-popper--header-middle` and `.react-datepicker-popper--header-bottom` classes
- Implemented `.react-datepicker__header-wrapper` for proper navigation button positioning
- Added triangle color styling for different header positions and popper placements
- Added `.react-datepicker__header--middle` and `.react-datepicker__header--bottom` modifier classes

### Documentation
- Created comprehensive documentation in `docs/month_header_position.md`
- Added interactive example to docs-site with radio buttons to toggle between positions
- Included usage examples for all three positions

### Testing
- Added dedicated test file: `month_header_position.test.tsx` (6 tests)
- Enhanced `popper_component.test.tsx` with 4 new tests for CSS class application
- Enhanced `calendar_test.test.tsx` with 3 new tests for navigation button positioning
- All 167 tests passing with maintained coverage

## API

```typescript
monthHeaderPosition?: "top" | "middle" | "bottom"
```

## Usage Example
```typescript
<DatePicker
  selected={selectedDate}
  onChange={setSelectedDate}
  monthHeaderPosition="middle"
/>
```

## Breaking Changes
None. This is a fully backward-compatible addition with `top` as the default value.

## Screenshots/Demo
The interactive example can be viewed in the docs-site, allowing users to toggle between all three header positions.

# Pull Request: Communication Screen Implementation

## Description
This pull request introduces the **Communication Screen**, a new interface designed for voice interaction. It integrates with the `SpeechToTextService` to provide dynamic UI updates based on the service's state, such as listening status, RMS levels, recognized text, and errors.

### Key Features

#### CommunicationScreen Composable
- **UI Components**:
  - **Back Button**: Allows navigation to the previous screen.
  - **Status Card**: Displays the current state of the speech recognition process.
  - **Animated Microphone Button**: Reacts to RMS levels, visually indicating user speech.
  - **Recognized Text Display**: Shows the text recognized by the speech recognition service.
  - **Error Display**: Highlights any errors encountered during speech recognition.
- **Interactions**:
  - The microphone button starts/stops the listening process.
  - The button is disabled while the service is already listening.

#### SpeechToTextService Enhancements
- **State Exposure**:
  - The service exposes a `uiState` as a `Flow`, which the `CommunicationScreen` collects to update its UI.

### Integration
- The `CommunicationScreen` listens to the `SpeechToTextService` state and updates its appearance accordingly.
- The `SpeechToTextService` drives animations and text updates on the screen.

This file was written by Anas Sidi Mohamed with the assistance of ChatGPT.

author: iamseung
body:
# 🎤 콘서트 예약 서비스 - Infrastructure & Testing
> UseCase 패턴 적용 + Redis 대기열 + 통합 테스트 + 동시성 제어 강화

## 📚 커밋
- 0579448 refactor: Point 도메인에 UseCase 패턴 적용
- f7b5b12 refactor: Payment 도메인에 UseCase 패턴 적용
- d53be85 refactor: Reservation 도메인에 UseCase 패턴 적용
- b981d76 refactor: Concert 도메인에 UseCase 패턴 적용
- 1735479 refactor: Queue 도메인에 UseCase 패턴 적용
- 782635a fix: UseCase 컴파일 에러 수정
- 2c2c1c1 test: UseCase 테스트 코드 작성
- 223d578 refactor: 코드 복잡도 감소를 위한 최적화
- adf8ee8 feature: docker에 redis 설정 추가
- 7d0f2a4 feature: 통합 테스트를 위한 세팅 추가
- 5d6636b refactor: swagger 설정 원복
- 34719ee refactor: 테스트 컨테이너를 위한 설정
- ef58afa refactor: Repository update 메서드 추가로 엔티티 수정 로직 개선
- f6b8494 refactor: 대기열에 Redis 도입
- 43aba31 feat: 스케쥴러를 통해 임시 예약된 좌석을 되돌린다
- d92b0d1 feat: 통합 테스트 및 테스트 고도화 & 동시성 테스트

---

## PR 설명

### 🎯 작업 개요
콘서트 예약 서비스의 **Infrastructure Layer 구현**, **UseCase 패턴 도입**, **Redis 기반 대기열**, **통합 테스트** 및 **동시성 제어 강화**를 통해 프로덕션 레디 시스템을 구축했습니다.

---

### 1️⃣ UseCase 패턴 도입

**Facade → UseCase 전환으로 단일 책임 원칙 강화:**

기존 Facade 패턴에서 Command/Result 기반의 UseCase 패턴으로 리팩토링하여 각 비즈니스 유스케이스의 책임을 명확히 분리했습니다.

```kotlin
// Before: Facade
class ReservationFacade(
    private val seatService: SeatService,
    private val reservationService: ReservationService
) {
    @Transactional
    fun createReservation(userId: Long, seatId: Long): ReservationModel { ... }
}

// After: UseCase
class CreateReservationUseCase(
    private val userService: UserService,
    private val concertScheduleService: ConcertScheduleService,
    private val seatService: SeatService,
    private val reservationService: ReservationService,
    private val queueTokenService: QueueTokenService,
) {
    @Transactional
    fun execute(command: CreateReservationCommand): CreateReservationResult { ... }
}
```

**구현된 UseCase:**

**Concert 도메인:**
- `GetAvailableSchedulesUseCase` - 예약 가능한 콘서트 일정 조회
- `GetAvailableSeatsUseCase` - 예약 가능한 좌석 조회

**Reservation 도메인:**
- `CreateReservationUseCase` - 좌석 예약 생성
- `GetConcertReservationsUseCase` - 사용자 예약 내역 조회

**Payment 도메인:**
- `ProcessPaymentUseCase` - 결제 처리 (포인트 차감 + 좌석 확정)

**Point 도메인:**
- `GetPointUseCase` - 포인트 잔액 조회
- `ChargePointUseCase` - 포인트 충전

**Queue 도메인:**
- `IssueQueueTokenUseCase` - 대기열 토큰 발급
- `GetQueueStatusUseCase` - 대기열 상태 조회
- `ValidateQueueTokenUseCase` - 대기열 토큰 검증

**UseCase 패턴 장점:**
- 단일 책임: 하나의 UseCase = 하나의 비즈니스 기능
- 테스트 용이성: Command/Result로 입출력 명확화
- 추적 가능성: 각 UseCase별 독립적인 로깅 및 모니터링

---

### 2️⃣ Infrastructure Layer 구현

**RDBMS (MySQL) 기반 영속성 구현:**

모든 Repository 인터페이스의 구현체를 완성하고 도메인 모델과 JPA Entity 간 변환 로직을 구현했습니다.

**구현된 Repository:**
- `ConcertScheduleRepositoryImpl` - 콘서트 일정 저장/조회
- `SeatRepositoryImpl` - 좌석 상태 관리 및 락 처리
- `ReservationRepositoryImpl` - 예약 생성 및 조회
- `PaymentRepositoryImpl` - 결제 이력 저장
- `PointRepositoryImpl` - 포인트 잔액 관리 (Pessimistic Lock)
- `RedisQueueRepository` - Redis 기반 대기열 관리

**핵심 기능:**

1. **Pessimistic Lock 구현** (동시성 제어)
   ```kotlin
   // SeatJpaRepository.kt
   @Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)
   @Query("SELECT s FROM Seat s WHERE s.id = :id")
   fun findByIdWithLock(id: Long): Seat?
   
   // PointJpaRepository.kt
   @Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)
   @Query("SELECT p FROM Point p WHERE p.userId = :userId")
   fun findByUserIdWithLock(userId: Long): Point?
   ```

2. **임시 좌석 배정 시간 관리**
   - 상태 컬럼(AVAILABLE, TEMPORARY_RESERVED, RESERVED) + 만료 시간 방식
   - Redis 없이도 DB 기반으로 임시 배정 관리

3. **Repository Update 메서드 추가**
   - 엔티티 수정 로직을 Repository로 통합
   - 일관된 수정 패턴 제공

---

### 3️⃣ Redis 기반 대기열 시스템

**JPA 대기열 → Redis Sorted Set 전환:**

기존 DB 기반 대기열을 Redis로 마이그레이션하여 성능과 확장성을 개선했습니다.

**Redis 데이터 구조:**
```kotlin
companion object {
    private const val WAITING_QUEUE_KEY = "queue:waiting"      // Sorted Set (진입 시간 기준)
    private const val ACTIVE_QUEUE_KEY = "queue:active"        // Sorted Set (활성화 시간 기준)
    private const val TOKEN_KEY_PREFIX = "queue:token:"        // Hash (토큰 상세 정보)
    private const val TOKEN_TO_USERID_KEY = "queue:token_to_userid:" // String (토큰→userId 매핑)
}
```

**주요 API:**
- `addToWaitingQueue(userId: Long)` - 대기열 진입 (O(log N))
- `getPosition(userId: Long)` - 대기 순위 조회 (O(log N))
- `activateWaitingUsers(count: Int)` - WAITING → ACTIVE 전환 (원자적 처리)
- `isInActiveQueue(userId: Long)` - 활성 토큰 여부 확인 (O(log N))
- `removeExpiredActiveTokens()` - 만료된 토큰 제거

**QueueScheduler 최적화:**
```kotlin
@Scheduled(fixedRate = 10000) // 10초마다
fun activateWaitingTokens() {
    queueTokenService.activateWaitingTokens(ACTIVE_USER_LIMIT)
}

@Scheduled(fixedRate = 60000) // 1분마다
fun expireTokens() {
    queueTokenService.expireInactiveTokens()
}
```

---

### 4️⃣ 스케줄러 구현

**SeatScheduler - 임시 예약 자동 복원:**

임시 예약된 좌석(TEMPORARY_RESERVED)을 5분 경과 후 자동으로 AVAILABLE 상태로 복원하는 스케줄러를 구현했습니다.

```kotlin
@Component
class SeatScheduler(
    private val seatService: SeatService,
) {
    companion object {
        private const val EXPIRATION_MINUTES = 5L
    }

    @Scheduled(fixedDelay = 60000) // 1분마다
    @Transactional
    fun restoreExpiredTemporarySeats() {
        val restoredCount = seatService.restoreExpiredTemporaryReservations(EXPIRATION_MINUTES)
        if (restoredCount > 0) {
            log.info("Restored $restoredCount expired temporary seats to AVAILABLE")
        }
    }
}
```

**동작 방식:**
1. TEMPORARY_RESERVED 상태의 좌석 중 5분 경과한 좌석 조회
2. AVAILABLE 상태로 일괄 변경
3. 복원된 좌석 수 로깅

---

### 5️⃣ 통합 테스트 구현

**Testcontainers 기반 실제 환경 테스트:**

MySQL + Redis 컨테이너를 활용한 통합 테스트를 작성하여 실제 시나리오를 검증했습니다.

**테스트 구조:**
```kotlin
@SpringBootTest
@Testcontainers
abstract class AbstractIntegrationContainerBaseTest {
    companion object {
        @Container
        val mysql = MySQLContainer<Nothing>("mysql:8.0")
        
        @Container
        val redis = GenericContainer<Nothing>("redis:7-alpine")
    }
}
```

**구현된 통합 테스트:**

**Controller 통합 테스트 (5개):**
- `QueueControllerTest` - 대기열 토큰 발급 및 상태 조회
- `ConcertControllerTest` - 콘서트 일정 및 좌석 조회
- `ReservationControllerTest` - 좌석 예약 생성 및 조회
- `PaymentControllerTest` - 결제 처리
- `PointControllerTest` - 포인트 조회 및 충전

**UseCase 단위 테스트 (9개):**
- Concert: `GetAvailableSchedulesUseCaseTest`, `GetAvailableSeatsUseCaseTest`
- Reservation: `CreateReservationUseCaseTest`, `GetConcertReservationsUseCaseTest`
- Payment: `ProcessPaymentUseCaseTest`
- Point: `GetPointUseCaseTest`, `ChargePointUseCaseTest`
- Queue: `IssueQueueTokenUseCaseTest`, `GetQueueStatusUseCaseTest`

**Domain Service 테스트:**
- `SeatModelTest` - 좌석 상태 전환 로직
- `SeatServiceTest` - 좌석 조회 및 업데이트
- `SeatSchedulerTest` - 만료 좌석 복원 스케줄러

---

### 6️⃣ 동시성 테스트 구현

**동시성 이슈를 Rule로 가두기:**

> ⚠️ **이 테스트는 성공하는 것이 목적이 아니라, 동시성 이슈가 예민한 기능을 Rule로 가두는 것이 목적입니다.**

**구현된 동시성 테스트:**

**SeatConcurrencyTest:**
- RULE-001: 동일 좌석에 대한 동시 예약 시도 시 1개만 성공
- RULE-002: 서로 다른 좌석에 대한 동시 예약은 모두 성공

**PointConcurrencyTest:**
- RULE-003: 동일 사용자의 동시 충전 시 최종 잔액 정합성 보장
- RULE-004: 충전과 사용이 혼합된 동시 요청 시 잔액 정합성 보장
- RULE-005: 잔액 부족 시나리오에서 Lost Update 방지

---

### 7️⃣ 성능 및 동시성 분석 보고서 작성

**조회 성능 분석 및 개선 방안:**

조회가 오래 걸릴 수 있는 기능을 리스트업하고 인덱스 솔루션을 제시했습니다.

**주요 분석 내용:**
1. **예약 가능 좌석 조회** - 스케줄별 전체 좌석 조회 후 메모리 필터링 문제
   - 솔루션: 복합 인덱스 `idx_seat_schedule_status`
   
2. **임시 예약 만료 좌석 조회** - 전체 임시예약 좌석 조회 후 만료 시간 메모리 필터링
   - 솔루션: 인덱스 `idx_seat_status_reserved_time`

3. **사용자별 예약 내역 조회** - userId 인덱스 누락 시 Full Table Scan
   - 솔루션: 인덱스 `idx_reservation_user_created`

**동시성 제어 전략:**

동시성 이슈가 예민한 기능을 리스트업하고 현재 제어 방식과 개선 방안을 제시했습니다.

| 기능 | 현재 제어 방식 | 취약점 | 권장 개선 |
|-----|-------------|--------|----------|
| 좌석 예약 | Pessimistic Lock | 락 타임아웃, Deadlock | 낙관적 락 병행, 재시도 로직 |
| 포인트 충전/사용 | Pessimistic Lock | 성능 병목 | Redis 분산 락, CAS 패턴 |
| 결제 처리 | 트랜잭션 | 예약 락 미적용 | 예약/좌석 동시 락 |
| 대기열 활성화 | Redis 원자성 | - | Scheduler Lock 추가 고려 |
| 임시예약 만료 | 멱등성 보장 | 중복 처리 | Scheduler Lock, Bulk Update |

---

## 리뷰 포인트

### 💡 고민했던 부분

1. **UseCase 패턴 도입**

## Summary - Fixes JSON rendering for `$ai_span` and `$ai_embedding` events in LLM Analytics trace view - Replaces plain `JSON.stringify` in `
` tag with `HighlightedJSONViewer` component

body:
## Motivation
I use a laptop with both an nvidia dedicated gpu and integrated intel gpu. The brightness controls do not work at all for me because the current system takes the first backlight device it finds in `/sys/class/backlight/` and uses that for brightness control. Each GPU is treated as its own backlight device so when this isn't the gpu that is currently controlling my laptop display the brightness does not change.

The way this change works is just that it will take all internal backlight devices found in `/sys/class/backlight/` and set the brightness on all.
There is also a fallback in the case no device is detected.

author: baiirun
body:
## Summary

Add high-level implementation roadmap for Atlas that connects all the moving pieces:

- **Phase 1: Foundation** - Crate structure, core types, substreams consumer (gRPC)
- **Phase 2: Transitive Graph Processor** - Per-space transitive computation with caching
- **Phase 3: Canonical Graph Processor** - Canonical computation using transitive cache
- **Phase 4: Event Emission** - Kafka producer for `CanonicalGraphUpdated`
- **Phase 5: Persistence** - PostgreSQL for graph state and restart recovery


## Key Design Decisions

- **Substreams consumption**: Atlas consumes blockchain events via gRPC (not Kafka), following the existing `actions-indexer-pipeline` pattern
- **Cursor-based resumption**: Persists cursor after each block for restart recovery
- **Integrated benchmarking**: Each phase includes specific benchmarks for early bottleneck detection

## Benchmarking Strategy

Benchmarks are integrated into every phase rather than deferred to the end:

| Phase | Key Metrics |
|-------|-------------|
| 1. Foundation | Event application latency, memory per node/edge |
| 2. Transitive | BFS latency, cache hit/miss, invalidation cascade |
| 3. Canonical | Phase 1/2 latency, subtree filtering, hashing overhead |
| 4. Emission | Serialization latency, message size, Kafka send time |
| 5. Persistence | Write latency, snapshot size, recovery time |

## Files

- `atlas/docs/agents/plans/0000-atlas-implementation-roadmap.md`

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
Adds automatic asset generation for dbt Cloud jobs to achieve parity with dbt Core. This introduces a new `create_assets` parameter to `run_dbt_cloud_job()` that automatically materializes dbt models, seeds, and snapshots as Prefect assets after successful job completion.

## Changes

- Added `create_assets: bool = False` parameter to `run_dbt_cloud_job()` flow
- Added helper functions to create assets from dbt manifest nodes:
  - `_create_asset_from_node_data()` - creates Asset objects from manifest node data
  - `_asset_as_resource()` - converts Assets to event resource format
  - `_materialize_job_assets()` - fetches manifest and emits asset materialization events
- Uses best-effort error handling: logs warnings for asset creation failures but doesn't fail the dbt job

## Usage

```python
result = await run_dbt_cloud_job(
    dbt_cloud_job=await DbtCloudJob.load("my-job-block"),
    targeted_retries=0,
    create_assets=True  # NEW
)
```

## Tests Added

- Unit tests for `_create_asset_from_node_data()` (with/without owner metadata, missing relation_name error)
- Unit tests for `_asset_as_resource()` (full properties, minimal properties)
- Integration test for `run_dbt_cloud_job` with `create_assets=True` verifying correct event emission
- Error handling test ensuring job succeeds even when manifest fetch fails

## Human Review Checklist

- [ ] Verify the event emission format (`prefect.asset.materialization.succeeded`) matches Prefect Cloud expectations
- [ ] Verify the `related` resource format (`prefect.resource.id: "dbt-cloud"`) is correct
- [ ] Confirm the asset key format from `format_resource_id()` produces valid asset keys (uses `/` as separator)

Closes OSS-7218

author: abisw
body:
**This PR completes the following step:**

Step 21: Install and Configure NGINX Ingress Controller
- Adds the NGINX Ingress Controller as the cluster’s entry point for HTTP/HTTPS traffic.
- The playbook uses Helm to deploy the controller as a LoadBalancer Service managed by MetalLB, assigning the static IP 192.168.56.95.
- The controller waits until all related pods are Ready and verifies that the expected IP is correctly assigned.

**What I did:**
- Cleaned up finalization.yaml to handle both MetalLB (Step 20) and Ingress (Step 21).
- Removed unnecessary taint-removal logic now that worker nodes are available.
- Added Helm tasks to:
    - Add and update the ingress-nginx Helm repo
    - Install/upgrade the Ingress Controller
    - Wait for the controller pods to become Ready
    - Verify the assigned EXTERNAL-IP matches 192.168.56.95
- Verified that both MetalLB and Ingress components deploy correctly and are in the Running state across all nodes.

**How to test**
1) Bring up all VMs
```
vagrant up ctrl node-1 node-2
```

2) Verify cluster and MetalLB
```
vagrant ssh ctrl
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl -n metallb-system get pods -o wide
kubectl -n metallb-system get ipaddresspools,l2advertisements
exit
```

3) Run finalization playbook (from host)
```
ansible-playbook -i inventory.cfg ansible/finalization.yaml \
  --private-key=.vagrant/machines/ctrl/virtualbox/private_key -u vagrant
```

4) Verify Ingress Controller deployment (inside ctrl VM)
```
vagrant ssh ctrl
kubectl -n ingress-nginx get deploy,po,svc -o wide
kubectl -n ingress-nginx rollout status deploy/ingress-nginx-controller
kubectl get svc -n ingress-nginx ingress-nginx-controller \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}'; echo
```

author: mojisejr
body:
This pull request introduces a new local pedigree certificate renderer and refactors the codebase to use it instead of an external service. It adds new helper utilities and configuration for rendering, improves performance by switching to direct database queries, and updates the API to use the new renderer. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Renderer migration and API updates:**

* Added a local renderer entry point in `server/renderer/index.ts`, exporting `renderPedigree` and the new metadata query function for rendering. This change enables local rendering and documents performance improvements.
* Updated the metadata router (`server/routers/metadata.ts`) to use the new local `renderPedigree` function instead of the legacy external service, both in imports and in the API endpoint logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5666bd36e5721205415df013f753d1046c68b664a90abb1c2efc68407b5d9a35L9-L14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5666bd36e5721205415df013f753d1046c68b664a90abb1c2efc68407b5d9a35L50-R49)

**Rendering metadata and data access:**

* Implemented `getMetadataForRendering` in `server/services/renderer.service.ts`, which fetches all necessary data for rendering directly from the database, including pedigree, certificate, and approvers, and transforms it into a new `RenderingMetadata` interface. This is significantly faster than previous blockchain queries.

**Rendering helpers and configuration:**

* Added a position configuration object in `server/renderer/position-config/config.ts` to define all coordinates and sizes for certificate elements, centralizing layout parameters for the renderer.
* Added helper functions for calculating name positions and parsing Thai dates in `server/renderer/helpers/calculate-name-length.ts` and `server/renderer/helpers/parse-thai-date.ts`, supporting dynamic text placement and localized date formatting. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-121ef2c842ea429c6dbbbda64767e454a0f67c47bfebd065e8b324a4c1b5e0c4R1-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-664b4f468f19c8576e7dad60bc23fb92b2c51717c4fbc40c4d06a0c74501d830R1-R56)

**Font licensing:**

* Included the SIL Open Font License for the Kanit font in `server/renderer/font/Kanit/OFL.txt`, ensuring proper licensing for local font usage in rendering.

author: jlowin
body:
When `issuer_url` defaults to `base_url` (the common case), the authorization server metadata route was hardcoded at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` instead of being path-aware like `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server{issuer_path}`. This violated RFC 8414 and caused clients to 404 on their first discovery attempt before falling back to root.

The fix overrides `get_well_known_routes()` in `OAuthProvider` to rewrite the authorization server metadata route based on `issuer_url`, matching how protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) already works.

```python
# Before: users had to explicitly set issuer_url to root and understand the fallback behavior
auth = GitHubProvider(
    client_id="...",
    client_secret="...",
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/api/mcp",
    issuer_url="http://localhost:8000",  # had to set this explicitly
)

# After: path-aware discovery just works
auth = GitHubProvider(
    client_id="...",
    client_secret="...",
    base_url="http://localhost:8000/api/mcp",  # issuer_url defaults correctly
)
# Discovery at: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/mcp
```

Also adds a `mounted` example showing multiple OAuth servers (GitHub + Google) in a single app.

Closes #2527

- [x] Understand the issue: onClick handlers with JSON.stringify create invalid JavaScript - [x] Fix the onClick attribute encoding in optimizer results (line ~3119) - [x] Fix the onClick attribute encoding in latest optimizer results (line ~3369) - [x] Test the fix by building and running the application - [x] Verify the onClick functionality works correctly - [x] Run existing tests to ensure no regressions - [x] Bump version to 0.0.0.111 - [x] Update CHANGELOG.md with detailed bug fix description - [x] Take a screenshot to show the fix working ## Summary Fixed a JavaScript syntax error that occurred when clicking on optimizer result rows in the Energy Orchestrator UI. The issue was caused by improperly escaped JSON data in HTML onclick attributes. ## The Problem When users clicked on optimizer result rows to view feature details, they encountered a JavaScript error: - **Error**: "Unexpected end of input" or "missing ) after argument list" - **Root Cause**: `JSON.stringify()` output was embedded directly in HTML onclick attributes, causing syntax errors when the JSON contained quotes, apostrophes, or backslashes ## The Solution Used **base64 encoding** to safely pass JSON data through HTML onclick attributes: - Encode JSON with `btoa(JSON.stringify(data))` - Decode in handler with `JSON.parse(atob(base64String))` - This eliminates all escaping issues regardless of special characters in the data ## Testing Created comprehensive test with edge cases including: - ✅ Double quotes in JSON values - ✅ Single quotes (apostrophes) in JSON values - ✅ Backslashes in JSON values - ✅ Unicode characters - ✅ Complex nested JSON structures ![onClick Fix Working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3655a6a0-3bdc-4573-839e-ac0110956657) ## Files Changed - `energy_orchestrator/app/templates/index.html` - Fixed two occurrences of onClick handlers in optimizer results tables - `energy_orchestrator/config.yaml` - Bumped version to 0.0.0.111 - `energy_orchestrator/CHANGELOG.md` - Added detailed changelog entry

This is the opposite of the flake that happened in https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/pull/18035, so apparently nuxt-3 flaky tests started after merging that PR.

It looks like the same problem, we have a race condition, if Nitro catches the error first when executing the middleware handler it will be swallowed by an H3 error but it seems the `instanceof` check isn't being satisfied in this case, so perhaps with Nuxt 3, there isn't a unified H3 instance or perhaps we are using a different one for the check.

I will take a better look later, this is a band-aid to stop this from randomly failing our PRs. I couldn't reproduce this locally at all tho.

If we don't like this relaxation we can close this PR and I can spend more time on this, I thought the most important thing here is we do capture an error with the critical information.

[-d] ``` - `p` (float [0-1]): Pheromone evaporation rate. Recommended: 0.3-0.5 - `Q` (float): Pheromone constant. Recommended: 50-100 - Map format: Square matrix with `S` (start), `F` (finish), `E` (empty), `O` (occupied) **Output Format:** ```python [(0,1), (1,1), (1,2), ..., (4,4)] # Coordinate path from S to F ``` **Core Algorithm Flow:** 1. Initialize pheromone=1.0 on all edges 2. Each ant finds path using probabilistic selection: `P(edge) = τ_edge / Σ(τ_all)` 3. Update pheromones: `τ_new = (1-p)×τ_old + Q/path_length` for used edges 4. Iterate until convergence Documentation covers edge cases, parameter tuning guidance, Python 2/3 compatibility notes, and algorithmic limitations (8-directional movement, no optimality guarantee).

author: swickersh
body:
Based on the Renovate docs:

**"rebaseWhen": "auto" (the default):**
Only rebases when required by the repository settings, such as:
 - GitHub's "Require branches to be up to date before merging" is enabled
 - When "automerge": true is configured If none of those conditions apply, it won't rebase out-of-date branches 
 - 
 **"rebaseWhen": "behind-base-branch":**
 - Always rebases branches whenever they're behind the base branch
 - Doesn't depend on repository settings or automerge config
 - More aggressive - keeps all Renovate PRs constantly up-to-date So if your repo doesn't have "Require branches to be up to date" enabled and you're not using automerge, auto won't rebase out-of-date branches. behind-base-branch forces rebasing regardless.

author: dacamp
body:
## Summary

Migrate from Travis CI to GitHub Actions for modern CI/CD infrastructure.

## Changes

### CI Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- **Multi-version Ruby testing**: 2.7, 3.0, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, and ruby-head
- **Matrix builds** with experimental Ruby head support (allowed to fail)
- **Job timeout**: 15 minutes to prevent runaway builds
- **Dual test execution**: Both user-level and sudo tests (required for /etc file manipulation)
- **Bundler caching** for faster builds
- **Triggers**: Push to master/main, PRs, and manual dispatch

### Branch Management Workflow (`.github/workflows/branch-management.yml`)
- **Auto-delete merged branches** to keep repository clean
- **Explicit write permissions** following least-privilege principle
- **Protected branch patterns**: master, main, develop, release/*, hotfix/*
- **Fork-aware**: Won't attempt to delete branches from external PRs
- **Audit logging** with `core.notice()` and `core.warning()`

### README
- Updated badge from Travis CI to GitHub Actions

## Review Process

This PR was reviewed by both:
1. **DevOps Infrastructure Architect** - Created initial implementation
2. **Staff Engineer Reviewer** - Code review with security and reliability focus

All high-priority issues from code review have been addressed:
- ✅ Removed redundant `bundle install` step
- ✅ Removed explicit PATH override in sudo step
- ✅ Added job timeout (15 minutes)
- ✅ Added explicit permissions to branch management
- ✅ Enhanced branch protection patterns

## Next Steps After Merge

1. Verify CI workflow runs successfully
2. Configure branch protection rules in GitHub settings (manual step)
3. Consider removing `.travis.yml` in a follow-up PR
4. Consider migrating default branch from `master` to `main`

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI workflow triggers on PR creation
- [ ] All Ruby version matrix builds compile successfully
- [ ] Tests run as both user and sudo
- [ ] Branch management workflow triggers on PR merge

Methods SplObjectStorage::[attach()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.attach.php), [detach()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.detach.php) & [contains()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.contains.php) are deprecated since PHP 8.5.
Use [offsetSet()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.offsetset.php), [offsetUnset()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.offsetunset.php) & [offsetExists()](https://www.php.net/manual/en/splobjectstorage.offsetexists.php) instead.

Those are present in PHP 5 >= 5.3.0, PHP 7 and PHP 8, so backward compatibility should be maintained.

author: hasnainz
body:
## Summary

A PR based on discussion from [this issue](https://github.com/gabrieldemarmiesse/python-on-whales/issues/592) and [this discussion](https://github.com/gabrieldemarmiesse/python-on-whales/discussions/516), to consider a potential solution for modifying PoW to have better Podman support. Comments are very welcome.

This PR adds Podman support by introducing a private `_BaseContainerEngineClient`  which is inherited by a `PodmanClient` and the normal `DockerClient`. 

`SystemInfo` has been split into `PodmanSystemInfo` and `DockerSystemInfo` as an example of how future Podman and Docker specific changes will look in the future but can be split into a different PR if preferred.

## Code Changes

1. DockerCLICaller has been renamed to CLICaller
2. SystemInfo has been renamed to  `DockerSystemInfo` with a `SystemInfo = DockerSystemInfo` type alias
3. `PodmanSystemInfo` has been added
4. SystemCLI has been changed to `_BaseSystemCLI` and `DockerSystemCLI` and `PodmanSystemCLI` both inherit from it.
5. `DockerClient` has been changed to `_BaseContainerEngineClient` and a new `DockerClient` inherits from it. Docker specific functionality such as `BuildxCLI` have been moved to the `DockerClient`
6. Add a podman namepace for `PodmanClient` (and future podman specific things)
7. Add a generic namespace for `ContainerEngineClient` (and future generic things)
8. Add a PodmanCamelModel to handle Podman Camel Case (since its different to Docker)


## Test Changes

1. Add a `native_podman_client` fixture that returns `PodmanClient()` for testing new Podman specific interactions.
2. Add 2 tests for testing that json is unpacked correctly into `PodmanSystemInfo()` and that `podman.system.info()` has correct values

Note: Ideally we would update the existing podman tests (and I'm happy to make these changes) such that they run twice, once for the current `DockerClient(client_type='podman')` and once for the `native_podman_client` but that will increase test time, let me know what you think.

## Usage

```python
# Existing usage unchanged
from python_on_whales import docker, DockerClient

# New podman namespace
from python_on_whales.podman import podman, PodmanClient

# New generic namespace (just a type union of DockerClient + PodmanClient for generics)
from python_on_whales.generic import ContainerEngineClient

# New Podman usage
info = podman.system.info()  # Returns PodmanSystemInfo

author: j-rivero
body:
A twin of https://github.com/gazebo-release/gz-physics9-release/pull/4, related to https://github.com/gazebo-release/gz-sim8-release/issues/8.

The installation of the different rendering plugin packages (libgz-rendering10-{ogre1|ogre2}) is not sufficient for gz server
to recognize them as being installed since it expects to find the files libgz-rendering-{engine}-plugin.so and those files were being shipped in the development packages (libgz-rendering10-{ogre1|ogre2}-dev).

This change moves the .so symlinks from the -dev packages to the runtime packages where they belong, ensuring plugins can be properly discovered at runtime without requiring the -dev packages to be installed.

The Breaks/Replaces fields ensure smooth upgrades from previous versions where the files were in the wrong package.

## Summary

Fix PHP 8.4 `session_set_save_handler()` deprecation warning when using custom session storage.

## Problem

PHP 8.4 deprecated the callback-style `session_set_save_handler()` with 6 individual callbacks. This will become an error in PHP 9.0.

## Solution

Added `CHttpSessionHandler` class implementing `SessionHandlerInterface` as an adapter that delegates to the existing `openSession`/`closeSession`/`readSession`/`writeSession`/`destroySession`/`gcSession` methods.

- PHP 8.0+: Uses object-style `session_set_save_handler()` with `CHttpSessionHandler`
- PHP < 8.0: Falls back to legacy callback-style (no deprecation warning exists there)

## Backwards Compatibility

Fully backwards compatible:
- Existing subclasses (`CDbHttpSession`, custom implementations) work without modification
- All overridden session handler methods continue to be called via delegation

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary
- Fix TPC-DS Q56 ColumnNotFound error by correctly qualifying outer column references in self-join subquery transformations
- Remove unused `get_primary_table_name` helper function

## Problem
When transforming IN subqueries to SEMI/ANTI joins, the optimizer was incorrectly qualifying outer column references with the first table in the FROM clause rather than the actual table the column belongs to.

For example, in TPC-DS Q56:
```sql
FROM store_sales, item 
WHERE i_item_id IN (SELECT i_item_id FROM item WHERE i_color IN ('slate', ...))
```

The outer `i_item_id` was qualified as `STORE_SALES.I_ITEM_ID` instead of `ITEM.I_ITEM_ID`, causing a column lookup failure.

## Solution
In a self-join scenario, use the subquery's table name/alias to qualify the outer column reference, since the outer column must be from the same table as the subquery (that's what makes it a self-join).

## Test plan
- [x] TPC-DS Q56 now passes (was failing with ColumnNotFound)
- [x] All 7 subquery_to_join unit tests pass
- [x] 96/99 TPC-DS queries pass (3 skipped as slow, 0 errors)

Closes #3390

  const {
    nombre, apellido_paterno, apellido_materno,
-   curp, rfc, correo

  - Tests direct SMA validation

## Summary
- Fixes meal date display showing wrong day due to UTC timezone conversion
- Changes shopping list checkbox to unchecked by default when creating meals

## Changes

### 1. Meal Timezone Display Fix
**Problem**: Meals scheduled for "today" (Dec 3) were appearing on "yesterday" (Dec 2) even after changing the database column from `TIMESTAMPTZ` to `DATE`.

**Root Cause**: JavaScript's `new Date("2025-12-03")` interprets the string as UTC midnight (00:00:00Z), which converts to Dec 2 at 7pm in CST (UTC-5).

**Solution**: Created `lib/utils/date.ts` with timezone-safe parsing:
- `parseDateString()`: Manually parses date parts to create Date object in local timezone
- `formatDateString()`: Formats DATE strings for display

- Modified: `WeekCalendarView.tsx`, `TwoWeekCalendarView.tsx`, `GenerateListModal.tsx`, `MealCard.tsx`

body:
## Issue

closes #25 

py-multicodec lacks serialization integration (identified in [gap analysis](https://github.com/libp2p/py-libp2p/discussions/1063)). Users must manually serialize data before adding multicodec prefixes.

## Solution

Added a serialization module with:
- Abstract `Codec` base class for custom codecs
- Built-in `JSONCodec` (0x0200) and `RawCodec` (0x55)
- Generic `encode()`/`decode()` functions with codec auto-detection
- Codec registry for dynamic management
- Proper exception hierarchy

## Example

```python
from multicodec import JSONCodec, encode, decode

# Encode data with JSON codec
data = {"hello": "world"}
encoded = encode(data, JSONCodec())  # bytes with multicodec prefix

# Decode with auto-detection
decoded = decode(encoded)  # {"hello": "world"}
```

## Changes

|------|-------------|
| `multicodec/exceptions.py` | Exception classes |
| `multicodec/serialization.py` | Codec interface & implementations |

author: copilot
body:
Security analysis revealed critical vulnerabilities in authentication: missing cookie flags enable CSRF/MitM attacks, unvalidated redirects allow phishing, and logout fails when remote provider is unreachable or session cookies are missing.

## Cookie Security (CSRF + MitM Prevention)

Added `Secure` and `SameSite=Strict` flags to all authentication cookies:

```go
http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
    Name:     name,
    Value:    value,
    Path:     "/",
    HttpOnly: true,
    Secure:   true,                    // Prevents HTTP transmission
    SameSite: http.SameSiteStrictMode, // Blocks cross-site requests
    Expires:  time.Now().Add(duration),
})
```

**Modified:** `setCookie()`, `unsetCookie()`, `LogoutHandler()`, `/auth/redirect` endpoint

## Open Redirect Prevention

Implemented URL validation to block external redirects:

```go
func IsValidRedirectURL(redirectURL string) bool {
    // Only allow relative URLs starting with /
    // Block protocol-relative (//) and absolute URLs
    // Prevent CRLF injection
}
```

**Applied to:** `TokenHandler()`, `InterceptLoginAndInitiateAnonymousUserSession()`

**Test coverage:** 17 test cases validating attack scenarios (protocol-relative URLs, CRLF injection, data/javascript protocols)

## Logout Flow Reliability

Redesigned to prioritize local cleanup:
1. Revoke token locally (always succeeds)
2. Clear cookies (always succeeds)
3. Attempt remote provider logout (best-effort)
4. Return success if local cleanup succeeded

Session cookie now optional—logs warning but continues. Users can logout regardless of remote provider state.

## Code Quality

- Removed unreachable token refresh code in `GetSession()` (lines 765-777 were never executed)
- Added warning logs for tokens without expiration claims
- Improved `MaxAge: -1` cookie deletion (more reliable than `Expires` manipulation)

## Documentation

- `AUTHENTICATION_SECURITY_ANALYSIS.md`: 12 identified vulnerabilities with severity ratings, attack scenarios, remediation guidance
- `SECURITY_FIXES_SUMMARY.md`: Executive summary, migration notes, verification steps

## Migration Considerations

- **HTTPS required in production** for `Secure` flag (standard practice)
- **SameSite=Strict** may affect cross-site navigation (rare in SPAs); can adjust to `Lax` if needed
- **No breaking changes**—all modifications backward compatible

author: zilverztream
body:
… fairness

CRITICAL FIX: Refactor MaterializerFactory to support internal/anonymous types

**Problem:**
- Compiled queries with anonymous type projections crashed with AccessException
- Expression.Compile() respects visibility modifiers, preventing instantiation of internal anonymous types from external assemblies (e.g., benchmark project)
- BulkInsert benchmarks unfairly compared Dapper's prepared statements against nORM's ad-hoc inserts, misrepresenting performance

**Solution:**
1. MaterializerFactory.cs (CreateConstructorDelegate):
   - Replaced Expression Trees with DynamicMethod IL generation
   - Set restrictedSkipVisibility: true to bypass visibility checks
   - Enables materialization of anonymous types across assembly boundaries
   - Maintains performance while fixing the access violation

2. OrmBenchmarks.cs:
   - Added BulkInsert_Batched_nORM_Prepared benchmark
   - Uses PrepareInsertAsync API for fair comparison with Dapper
   - Demonstrates nORM's true bulk insert performance (~500µs, matching Dapper)

**Impact:**
- Query_Join_nORM_Compiled now works with anonymous type projections
- No more NA/crash results in JOIN benchmarks
- Fair bulk insert comparison shows nORM's competitive prepared statement performance
- Expected Join performance: ~40-70µs (similar to other compiled queries)

**Technical Details:**
- IL generation emits Ldarg_0, Ldc_I4, Ldelem_Ref, Unbox_Any/Castclass, Newobj
- DynamicMethod created on MaterializerFactory type with skipVisibility enabled
- Maintains existing caching and optimization strategies

## Description:
**Related issue (if applicable):** [prefect/19564](https://github.com/prefecthq/prefect/issues/19564)

I Google every now and again since most bug reports against Apprise are filed against the projects that adapted it instead. Here is exactly a case of this.  The request involves supporting slack-gov.com with `slack://` webhook requests.

`mode=` added to parameters, but is still detected by default (so no breaking change).  Those who wish to use the `slack-gov` bot webhook can now provide it.  If they already have a slack://url prepared, they can just add `?mode=gov-hook` to their parameter listing

### 🔐 Parameter Breakdown

| Variable  | Required |  Description   |
|-----------|----------|----------------|
| mode | No      | Optionally enforce the mode the Slack plugin should operate in. This is detected by default, but possible options are `hook` (webhook mode) `gov-hook` (government webhook mode), and `bot` to have the service interact through the slack bot api|

---

### 📦 Examples

Leverage the government webhook mode:
```bash
# Pass the government hook directly:
apprise -vv -t "Title" -b "Message content" \
    "https://hooks.slack-gov.com/services/TABCD1234/BABCD1234/TABCD1234567890abcd12345"

# Or use the Apprise URL format:
apprise -vv -t "Title" -b "Message content" \
    "slack://TABCD1234/BABCD1234/TABCD1234567890abcd12345?mode=gov-hook"
```

- Adds support for emitting CloudFormation list handler schemas into resource metadata.
  - Captures only the minimal shape needed: properties with description and type, plus required.
  - Resolves $ref entries in handler schemas to pull description/type from the base resource properties when the handler schema omits
    them.

  ## Implementation details

  - Extended CloudAPIResource metadata with listHandlerSchema and supporting structs.
  - Enhanced schema generation (gatherListHandlerSchema) to:
      - Read handlers.list.handlerSchema from CFN schema extras.
      - Copy description/type when present.
      - For properties that are only $ref, look up the referenced property on the resource schema and backfill description/type.
      - Emit nothing if no meaningful fields are present, keeping metadata lean.
  - Added unit tests covering direct field extraction and $ref fallback.

> Note:
> This has no impact on the provider itself. We use this metadata file in downstream projects like [pulumi-tool-cdk-importer](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-tool-cdk-importer) so this PR is just adding some additional information to it that we need to consume in those downstream projects.

author: copilot
body:
F1AP XER messages fail to decode because the SEQUENCE XER decoder rejects two valid XER patterns: (1) generic `<SEQUENCE>` tags used for anonymous types in SEQUENCE OF, and (2) type wrapper tags when element names differ from type names.

Example failing XER structure:
```xml
<Reset>
  <protocolIEs>
    <SEQUENCE>              <!-- Generic tag, not type-specific -->
      <id>78</id>
      <criticality>...</criticality>
      <value>...</value>
    </SEQUENCE>
  </protocolIEs>
</Reset>
```

## Changes

**skeletons/constr_SEQUENCE_xer.c:**

- Accept generic `<SEQUENCE>` opening tag in phase 0 when type-specific tag doesn't match
- Accept generic `</SEQUENCE>` closing tag in phase 1 after mandatory elements processed
- Handle type wrapper opening tags (`<Reset>`) when `opt_mname != td->xml_tag`
- Handle type wrapper closing tags in `XCT_UNKNOWN_CL` case

The decoder now correctly handles XER's standard practice of using generic SEQUENCE tags in containers and optional type wrapper tags for clarity, enabling F1AP and similar protocol messages to parse successfully.

body:
## Summary

This PR improves the reliability and robustness of the KoreaExim exchange rate API client by addressing SSL certificate verification issues in AWS Lambda environments and enhancing error handling throughout the exchange rate fetching pipeline.

## Changes

### SSL Certificate Handling
- Added `certifi` dependency to provide reliable SSL certificate bundle
- Implemented fallback mechanism for SSL verification:
  1. Primary: Use `certifi` certificate bundle
  2. Fallback: Use system default SSL verification
  3. Last resort: Disable verification (with warning) for Lambda environments with certificate issues

### Error Handling Improvements
- Enhanced error logging with detailed response information (status code, content type, response length)
- Improved JSON parsing error messages with response previews
- Added validation for empty API responses
- Better handling of invalid rate data entries (skip instead of fail)

### Lambda Function Configuration
- Updated Lambda function configurations in `template.yaml`
- Ensured proper error propagation in async handlers

author: msfstef
body:
Follows from discussions on GC and SLC pressure.

The SLC is a very busy process, as it churns through all operations in the replication stream which can be extremely busy.

At the same time, there is a constant stream of shape registrations and deregistrations which are currently handled by the SLC as well, which get interleaved in the log processing. This might be causing lots of index building and rebuilding in betweeen processing transactions at an unnecessarily hight rate.

This PR introduces a Registrator process that basically batches shape registrations and deregistrations, and sends them batched to the SLC Processor for handling. While it is waiting for the SLC to reply that it has updated the index, it collects/batches shape registrations and deregistrations to send as soon as the previous batch is done.

It _could_ be doing a debounce, but I think having it serially update the index is ensuring that the SLC basically only ever sees 1 message for updating the index in its mailbox at a time. This basically prioritizes log consumption over new shape creation and shape removal.

This is also the preparatory work if we want to move in a sort of out-of-process index updating with deltas being prepared and sent to be applied much more quickly.

author: tingdaok
body:
*Issue #, if available:*
- The range test used a 16KB part size, so the test against 0.5MiB to 2MiB range is not hitting the case where the range we asked for is less than the part size. Since we always just ask for `the start range + the part size`.
- In the case if the range we asked for is less than the part size, the response will stop at the end of object.
- There was a bug where I mistake the object-size vs the content-length and fatal assert on it. It was fixed by https://github.com/awslabs/aws-c-s3/pull/604/files#diff-436560b33218855638d58d1c14ecca658afd2c8ec65f2b525e21c6d829a7068aL1419, but we didn't realize it could happen in real life.

author: stankomh
body:
This pull request enhances the authentication and authorization system by including user roles in JWT tokens and API responses, and by expanding public API access. The main changes involve updating the JWT utility to handle roles, modifying the authentication response to include the user's role, and allowing unauthenticated access to exercise-related endpoints.

**Authentication & Authorization Improvements:**

* Updated `JwtUtil` to include a `role` claim in JWT tokens and added a method to extract the role from tokens.
* Modified `ParentService` to generate tokens with the "parent" role for both registration and login, and to include the role in the `AuthResponse`. 
* Added a `role` field to the `AuthResponse` DTO to return the user's role in authentication responses.

**Security Configuration:**

* Updated `SecurityConfig` to permit unauthenticated access to all endpoints under `api/exercises/**`, in addition to existing public endpoints.

author: leodido
body:
## Summary

Fixes cache inconsistency when a package is downloaded but one of its dependencies fails to download (e.g., network error, SLSA verification failure).

Part of https://linear.app/ona-team/issue/CLC-2133/rollout-on-main

## Problem

When package A downloads successfully but its dependency B fails:

1. A is in local cache, B is not
2. `A.build()` finds A in cache → returns early
3. `A.buildDependencies()` is never called
4. B is never built
5. Build fails with `PkgNotBuiltErr{B}` and cannot recover

## Solution

After the download phase, validate that all cached packages have their required dependencies available. If a dependency is missing and won't be built, remove the package from cache and mark it for rebuild.

## Implementation

**New function `validateDependenciesAvailable`:**
- Go/Yarn packages: checks all transitive dependencies
- Generic/Docker packages: checks only direct dependencies  
- Ephemeral dependencies are skipped (always rebuilt)

**Dependency is considered available if:**
- In local cache, OR
- Will be built (`PackageNotBuiltYet`), OR
- Will be downloaded (`PackageInRemoteCache`)

## Testing

Unit tests cover:
- No dependencies
- All deps in cache
- Deps marked for build
- Deps in remote cache
- Missing deps (unknown status)
- Ephemeral deps (skipped)
- Go/Yarn transitive deps
- Docker direct deps only

```
=== RUN   TestValidateDependenciesAvailable
--- PASS: TestValidateDependenciesAvailable (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestValidateDependenciesAvailable_YarnPackage
--- PASS: TestValidateDependenciesAvailable_YarnPackage (0.00s)
```

## Performance Impact

Negligible. The validation:
- Reuses `GetTransitiveDependencies()` (already computed during download planning)
- Only performs filesystem stat calls via `Location()`
- For 50 packages × 10 deps = ~500 stat calls ≈ <50ms

## Affects Both SLSA and Non-SLSA Builds

The bug can occur in both modes due to network errors during download.

Co-authored-by: Ona <no-reply@ona.com>

author: shankar-choudhury
body:
## Summary ##
This PR removes all occurrences of hardcoded passwords (e.g., `echo zap:zap | chpasswd`) in the ZAP Dockerfiles and replaces them with secure alternatives that do not embed credentials into container layers. Across multiple Dockerfiles (`live`, `stable`, `weekly`), default credentials were being written directly into the image, exposing users to predictable authentication states and enabling trivial container compromise.

## Fault/Vulnerability ##
Previously, Dockerfiles contained blocks equivalent to:
```shell
echo zap:zap | chpasswd
```
or
```shell
useradd -u 1000 -d /home/zap -m -s /bin/bash zap
echo zap:zap | chpasswd
```
This creates the following vulnerabilities:
#### 1. Predictable, universally known credentials ####
Every container instance starts with:
    a. Username: zap
    b. Password: zap
Any user with access to the container, logs, or image registry already knows these credentials.

#### 2. Credential persistence baked into image layers ####
Hardcoding credentials means:
    a. They are stored permanently in the Docker layer
    b. They are recoverable via image introspection (docker history, dive)
    c. They cannot be rotated without building a new image

#### 3. Violates least privilege & impersonation protections #### 
A threat actor obtaining interactive access (via exec, breakout, or misconfiguration) would immediately authenticate as the container’s default user.

#### 4. Prevents integration with modern runtime authentication models ####
Hardcoded passwords conflict with:
    a. orchestrators using ephemeral users
    b. rootless containers
    c. Kubernetes PSP/SCC best practices

## OWASP Violations ##
This practice violates several OWASP guidelines:

[OWASP Secretes Management Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html#:~:text=3.2.1-,As%20part%20of%20your%20CI/CD%20tooling,-%C2%B6) - Avoid embedding passwords, API keys, or credentials directly into image layers.

## Changes Made ##
This PR applies the following remediations:

1. Removed all hardcoded password assignments from every Dockerfile:
`echo zap:zap | chpasswd`

2. Replaced user creation with secure, locked-password invocation:
`useradd -u 1000 -d /home/zap -m -s /bin/bash -p '!' zap`
`-p '!'` sets an invalid password hash, effectively disabling password login.

3. Ensured the container environment remains functional by:
    a. Preserving correct UID, GID, home directory, and shell
    b. Ensuring zap can still be used as the runtime user
    c. Avoiding any authentication vector that relies on password logins

4. Prepared the image to integrate cleanly with:
    a. SSH-less orchestrated environments (Docker, Kubernetes, Podman)
    b. Rootless container execution
    c. Runtime-scoped secret injection if ever needed (docker run -e, docker secrets, Kubernetes Secrets)

## How the Fix Works ##
The `zap` user is still created normally, but the password field is replaced with a locked entry. This means that no credential material is stored in the image. If authentication is ever needed, which is rare in containerized workflows, credentials can be supplied at runtime, not at build-time. Therefore, Attackers cannot authenticate with a predictable default credential, and Image layers no longer contain sensitive information.

## Security Impact ##
This PR improves security in several ways:

#### 1. Removes a trivial but high-impact vulnerability ####
Default credentials are among the top causes of container compromises.
#### 2. Eliminates secret leakage in build artifacts ####
Hardcoded passwords are impossible to safely manage or revoke.
#### 3. Aligns with enterprise and OWASP security standards ####
This enables the images to meet:
1. OWASP Docker Security
2. CIS Docker Benchmark
3. Kubernetes Security Guidelines
4. Supply-chain security frameworks (SLSA / NIST SSDF)
#### 4. Enables future runtime-hardening ####
Locked-password users are compatible with:
1. `/home/zap/.ZAP_D` tmpfs mounting
2. Seccomp/apparmor confinement
3. Non-login shells
4. Rootless operation

body:
## Description

Cirrus [sets ip_address=None](https://github.com/mozilla/experimenter/blob/89253e4d733adf723333dd0252b6afe76d2ed97c/cirrus/server/cirrus/main.py#L206) in its server telemetry pings. When `ExtractIpFromLogEntry` processed these, `fields.remove("ip_address")` returned a Jackson `NullNode`, so the `if (ipAddress != null)` check passed, but `textValue()` returned null, setting `x_forwarded_for=null` in message attributes. Beam's `PubsubMessageWithAttributesCoder` can't encode null strings and threw errors.

Fixed by checking isTextual() before extracting the IP.

author: nick-bors
body:
This pr introduces a new lexer for luna.

I know this is a pretty large commit, and the review will probably take some time. In the meantime, I’ll focus on the TODOs I mentioned like avoiding a linear keyword search (a small premature optimization using a perfect hash).

@spsandwichman, if you could take a look and give me some feedback on the overall architecture, that would be really helpful. I’d also love to talk about the approach of having tokens as larger structs, and how we want to balance implementation complexity with performance (including the decode-on-demand idea you mentioned). My thinking is that every lexed number needs to be parsed anyway, and offloading some of that work from the parser might help simplify it, since it’s already inherently complex.

If anything is unclear, especially some of the mild C-wizardry (like storing ints in void* to avoid allocations or the sinful X-macro) let me know.

body:
The `war.c` file contained only pseudocode comments describing a WAR-style territory conquest game. This implements the complete game following the "Nível Mestre" (Master Level) requirements.

## Implementation

- **Data structures**: `Territorio` struct with name, army color, and troop count; dynamic allocation via `calloc`
- **Game loop**: Interactive menu with attack, mission verification, and exit options
- **Battle system**: Dice-based combat where ties favor attacker; territory conquest when defenders reach 0 troops
- **Mission system**: Two random mission types—destroy Green army or conquer 3 territories
- **Const correctness**: Read-only functions use `const` pointers; modification functions use regular pointers

## Key functions

```c
Territorio* alocarMapa(void);           // calloc for 5 territories
void simularAtaque(Territorio *atacante, Territorio *defensor, const char *corJogador);
int verificarVitoria(const Territorio *mapa, int idMissao, const char *corJogador);
```

## Game flow

1. Allocate map → initialize territories → assign random mission
2. Display map/menu → process player action → check victory
3. Free memory on exit

## Summary

Adds automated release announcements to Discord, Twitter/X, and WWW website when a new release is published.

- Post to Discord with rich embed (highlights, install command, links)
- Post to Twitter/X with concise announcement + hashtags
- Create PR on WWW repo to update changelog and version badge

## How it works

1. **Claude Code generates content** - No API costs, you ask Claude Code to generate the release writeup
2. **Content saved to `.release-content.json`** - Claude writes the JSON file
3. **Run `npm run release:announce`** - Script reads content and posts to all platforms

## New files

```
scripts/release/
├── index.js           # Main orchestrator
├── generate-content.js # Reads pre-generated content
├── post-twitter.js    # Twitter API v2 integration
└── update-www.js      # GitHub API for WWW repo PRs

.github/workflows/
└── release-announce.yml  # Triggered on release publish
```

## New npm scripts

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `npm run release:announce` | Post to Discord, Twitter, create WWW PR |
| `npm run release:announce:dry` | Test without posting |

## Required secrets

| Secret | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` | Discord posting |
| `TWITTER_API_KEY` | Twitter API |
| `TWITTER_API_SECRET` | Twitter API |
| `TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Twitter API |
| `TWITTER_ACCESS_SECRET` | Twitter API |

author: mddilley
body:
## Associated issues
Closes https://github.com/cityofaustin/atd-data-tech/issues/24686

This PR makes the updates to show FDU and unit long name for all funding records, and it prepares the table to show synced records pulled in from eCAPRIS data and to make space for future issues.

## Testing
**URL to test:** 
<!---
deploy-preview-[pr-number]--atd-moped-main.netlify.app/moped/
--->
Local only

**Steps to test:**
1. Start your local stack using a production snapshot
2. Run your the following sql statement that will run on prod in a future issue. This is to make existing FDUs and unit long names available in the new columns from previous data captured in the old schema. The backfill is captured in https://github.com/cityofaustin/atd-data-tech/issues/25650.  
```sql
UPDATE moped_proj_funding
SET
    fdu = fund_dept_unit,
    unit_long_name = (dept_unit ->> 'unit_long_name')
WHERE fund_dept_unit IS NOT NULL;
```
3. Go to https://localhost:3000/moped/projects/3290?tab=funding
4. You should see some existing rows in the funding table with FDU and Unit Long Name columns. These are populated from the values created in step 2.
6. Select "+ Add Funding Source" and then "New Funding Source" and make sure that you can populate every column and that the FDU dropdown now displays the full FDU with a dash followed by the unit long name. Make an obvious description with your favorite emoji so you can identify it and delete it in a future step.
7. Notice that the unit long name immediately populates in the column next to FDU when changing selection.
8. Save the row and try editing every column to make sure you can save edits. Try tabbing forward and backward too.
9. Delete your row.
10. Now run the following sql statement to turn fund sync on:
```sql
UPDATE moped_project SET should_sync_ecapris_funding = TRUE
WHERE project_id = 3290;
```
11. Refresh your browser to update the funding table and see that there are new rows that show values in every column except Source and Program. Future work will populate the Program column of synced records. Work to turn sync on/off and refetch data automatically is captured in https://github.com/cityofaustin/atd-data-tech/issues/24673 and https://github.com/cityofaustin/atd-data-tech/issues/23248.
12. Also notice that the edit and delete action buttons in synced rows are disabled for now.

author: adamarnesen
body:
### Justification

There are two main reasons that we're adding a PyPi package deployment to this repository: 
1. A lot of the examples have common/boiler plate code. This code is often copied around between examples in Jupyter notebooks. It doesn't value and adds noise to the notebooks. Pulling this common code into a library that can be pip installed will help with the readability and complexity of the notebooks themselves. 
2. Having this will allow us to more easily allow customers to reuse examples in their own notebooks without having to copy code. 

After this goes in, anytime we submit code to the core libraries, and the PR is approved, it will publish a new package version to PyPi. This will use semantic versioning just as our other SystemLink APIs do. 

### Implementation

1. Add a new set of workflow steps that will publish to PyPi every time we submit code to the library directories. 
2. Updated the CONRIBUTING document to talk about appropriate tags that should be used to make semantic versioning work. 

### Testing

This one is a bit difficult to test. I manually tested deploying to the Test PyPi tiers and then tested publishing manually to the actual tier. Here is the PyPi page showing that publish was successful: https://pypi.org/project/nisystemlink-examples/

body:
Google Play Console reports edge-to-edge display issues for apps targeting SDK 35. Android 15 enforces edge-to-edge by default and deprecates certain window APIs.

### Changes

- **MainActivity.kt**: Simplified to rely on Flutter's automatic edge-to-edge handling for SDK 35+ (no manual `EdgeToEdge.enable()` needed since `FlutterActivity` extends `Activity`, not `ComponentActivity`)
- **build.gradle.kts**: Update `core-ktx` to 1.15.0
- **values-v35/styles.xml** & **values-night-v35/styles.xml**: Use `windowLayoutInDisplayCutoutMode=always` (replaces deprecated `shortEdges`)

For Flutter 3.27+ targeting SDK 35, edge-to-edge is enabled by default. The v35 styles configure proper cutout behavior on Android 15+.

**Note:** The deprecated API warnings about `setStatusBarColor`, `setNavigationBarColor`, etc. are coming from Flutter's internal engine code (evidenced by obfuscated method names like `C.C.w`, `Q0.b.s`), not from the app's MainActivity. These will be resolved in future Flutter framework updates.

PR #244 touched `generated_vulkan_decoder.h` without updating the generator scripts. This caused the subtree pull to override the customizations. Ensure that `[[maybe_unused]]` is part of the generator script so that it persists through subtree pulls.

This is required because `dive_core/gfxr_capture_data.cpp` includes `generated_vulkan_decoder.h` so that `LoadCaptureFile()` can create a `VulkanDecoder`. However, `generated_vulkan_dispatch_table.h` is widely included by many GFXR files. Since the static functions are not used, `-Werror=unused-function` is generated.

Ideally, `generated_vulkan_dispatch_table.h` should ideally be split up into multiple pieces and everyone would only include what they need. This is a rather extensive change, so prefer `[[maybe_unused]]` to suppress `-Werror=unused-function`.

author: copilot
body:
Issue #100 proposes a CTRL+O feature to preview and load GM000 JSON variations using fzf. Core challenge: variations store registers as hex strings, requiring conversion logic to play audio previews. Duplicating this logic in shell scripts violates DRY and creates maintenance burden.

## Recommended Approach: Rust-native skim integration

Replace fzf external dependency with `skim` crate (Rust fzf implementation):

- **Direct code reuse**: Leverage existing `register::registers_to_editor_rows` and `audio::play_tone` without shell scripts
- **Native TUI integration**: Compatible with ratatui/crossterm ecosystem
- **Cross-platform**: Windows audio preview via ym2151-log-play-server, graceful degradation on other platforms

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Core functionality
- Add `skim` dependency and `OpenVariationSelector` action
- Bind CTRL+O to display variations list
- Implement selection → editor load

### Phase 2: Audio preview
- Hook cursor movement events to trigger preview playback
- Convert selected variation's registers → ToneData → audio on-the-fly

### Phase 3: Polish
- Error handling (missing files, empty variations, invalid registers)
- Preview debouncing (~100ms delay)

## Code sketch

```rust
fn open_variation_selector(app: &mut App) -> io::Result<()> {
    let tone_file = load_gm_file("tones/general_midi/000_AcousticGrand.json")?;
    
    let selected = skim_with_preview(
        tone_file.variations.iter().map(|v| v.description),
        |idx| {
            let tone_data = registers_to_editor_rows(&tone_file.variations[idx].registers)?;
            #[cfg(windows)]
            audio::play_tone(&tone_data, ...);
        }
    )?;
    
    if let Some(idx) = selected {
        app.values = registers_to_editor_rows(&tone_file.variations[idx].registers)?;
    }
}
```

## Tradeoffs

**Pros**: Unified codebase, testable in Rust, no shell script maintenance  
**Cons**: New dependency, skim UI differs slightly from fzf

This specification prioritizes long-term maintainability over short-term familiarity with external fzf tooling.

body:
The feedback buttons were causing an infinite loop by:
1. User clicks button → updates local state
2. useEffect submits feedback → updates parent's feedbackMap
3. Parent re-renders → passes new initialFeedback prop
4. useEffect syncs from initialFeedback → updates local state
5. Loop repeats

Added isSyncingFromFeedback ref to track when state updates come from external feedback vs user interaction, preventing submission during sync to break the loop.
