<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Aufgabe
> 
> Erweitere die `.github/copilot-instructions.md` um Regeln für MessagePack Vererbung. Der Abschnitt "MessagePackObject Validierung" muss um die Vererbungs-Regeln ergänzt werden.
> 
> ## Zu ergänzender Inhalt
> 
> Füge nach dem bestehenden MessagePackObject Validierung Abschnitt (oder integriere es dort) folgende Regeln hinzu:
> 
> ```markdown
> ### MessagePack Vererbung (WICHTIG)
> 
> Bei Klassen die von anderen `[MessagePackObject]` Klassen erben:
> 
> 1. **Keys müssen fortlaufend sein über die Vererbungshierarchie:**
>    - Basisklasse startet bei `[Key(0)]`
>    - Abgeleitete Klasse startet bei **letzter Basis-Key + 1**
>    
>    ```csharp
>    // ✅ RICHTIG
>    [MessagePackObject]
>    public class EntityData
>    {
>        [Key(0)] public int Id { get; set; }
>        [Key(1)] public EntityType EntityType { get; set; }
>        [Key(2)] public float X { get; set; }
>        [Key(3)] public float Y { get; set; }
>        // Letzter Key: 3
>    }
>    
>    [MessagePackObject]
>    public class PlayerData : EntityData
>    {
>        // Startet bei Key(4) weil EntityData bei Key(3) endet!
>        [Key(4)] public string Username { get; set; }
>        [Key(5)] public float VelocityX { get; set; }
>        [Key(6)] public float VelocityY { get; set; }
>    }
>    ```
> 
> 2. **FALSCH - Keys überschneiden sich:**
>    ```csharp
>    // ❌ FALSCH - Key(0) kollidiert mit Basisklasse!
>    [MessagePackObject]
>    public class PlayerData : EntityData
>    {
>        [Key(0)] public string Username { get; set; }  // ❌ Kollidiert mit EntityData.Id!
>    }
>    ```
> 
> 3. **Prüf-Checkliste bei Vererbung:**
>    - [ ] Basisklasse hat `[MessagePackObject]`?
>    - [ ] Abgeleitete Klasse hat `[MessagePackObject]`?
>    - [ ] Letzter Key der Basisklasse ermittelt?
>    - [ ] Abgeleitete Klasse startet bei letzter Basis-Key + 1?
>    - [ ] Keine Key-Lücken oder Duplikate?
> 
> 4. **Fehlermeldung bei Verstoß:**
> 
>    > ⚠️ **MessagePack Vererbung - Key-Kollision**
>    > 
>    > Die Klasse `{ClassName}` erbt von `{BaseClassName}`, aber die Keys sind falsch:
>    > - `{BaseClassName}` verwendet Keys 0-{lastBaseKey}
>    > - `{ClassName}` muss bei Key({lastBaseKey + 1}) starten, startet aber bei Key({actualFirstKey})
>    > 
>    > **Korrektur:**
>    > ```csharp
>    > [MessagePackObject]
>    > public class {ClassName} : {BaseClassName}
>    > {
>    >     [Key({lastBaseKey + 1})]  // Nicht [Key(0)]!
>    >     public string FirstProperty { get; set; }
>    > }
>    > ```
> 
> 5. **Unterschied: Message vs. Daten-Klasse bei Vererbung:**
> 
>    | Typ | `INetworkMessage` | `MessageType` als Key(0) | Vererbungs-Keys |
>    |-----|-------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|
>    | Message-Klasse | ✅ Ja | ✅ Ja | Basis-Key + 1 |
>    | Daten-Klasse (Basis) | ❌ Nein | ❌ Nein | Startet bei Key(0) |
>    | Daten-Klasse (Abgeleitet) | ❌ Nein | ❌ Nein | Basis-Key + 1 |
> 
> 6. **Beispiel mit vollständiger Hierarchie:**
> 
>    ```
>    EntityData (Daten-Klasse, Basis)
>    ├── [Key(0)] int Id
>    ├── [Key(1)] EntityType EntityType
>    ├── [Key(2)] float X
>    └── [Key(3)] float Y
>             ↓
>    PlayerData : EntityData (Daten-Klasse, Abgeleitet)
>    ├── erbt [Key(0-3)] von EntityData
>    ├── [Key(4)] string Username      ← Startet bei 4!
>    ├── [Key(5)] float VelocityX
>    └── [Key(6)] float VelocityY
>             ↓
>    WorldState (Message-Klasse, nutzt PlayerData)
>    ├── [Key(0)] MessageType Type     ← Message hat MessageType!
>    ├── [Key(1)] long ServerTime
>    └── [Key(2)] List<PlayerData> Players
>    ```
> ```
> 
> ## Akzeptanzkriterien
> 
> - [ ] Vererbungs-Regeln sind dokumentiert
> - [ ] Beispiel für korrekte Vererbung ist enthalten
> - [ ] Beispiel für falsche Vererbung (Key-Kollision) ist enthalten
> - [ ] Prüf-Checkliste für Reviews ist enthalten
> - [ ] Fehlermeldung-Template für Copilot ist enthalten
> - [ ] Unterschied Message vs. Daten-Klasse bei Vererbung ist erklärt
> - [ ] Visuelles Beispiel der Hierarchie ist enthalten


</details>

body:
Excel loader was breaking at first blank row, ignoring all questions below it. Section headers (e.g., "Section 2: Cloud Computing") also stopped processing.

## Changes

- **Skip blank rows**: Continue iterating instead of breaking on empty cells
- **Detect section headers**: Heuristic-based detection for common patterns:
  - Section prefixes (`Section 1:`, `Part A:`, `Chapter 3:`)
  - Decorated text (`--- Category ---`, `=== Section ===`)
  - All uppercase short text
  - Numbered sections without question marks
- **Track row indices**: Store original Excel row numbers in `SheetData.row_indices` so answers write back to correct positions

```python
# Before: stops at row 4
# Row 2: Question 1  →  processed
# Row 3: Question 2  →  processed  
# Row 4: (blank)     →  BREAK
# Row 5: Question 3  →  never processed

# After: skips blanks and headers, tracks original positions
questions = ["Question 1", "Question 2", "Question 3"]
row_indices = [2, 3, 5]  # answers written to correct rows
```

## Files
- `src/excel/loader.py`: Modified loading logic, added `_is_section_header()`
- `src/utils/data_types.py`: Added `row_indices: Optional[List[int]]` to `SheetData`
- `tests/unit/test_excel_blank_rows.py`: 9 new tests for header detection and blank row handling

author: akatz-ai
body:
## Summary

This PR replaces the separate `publish-core.yml` and `publish-cli.yml` workflows with a unified `publish.yml` workflow that implements lockstep versioning for both packages.

**Key changes:**
- Both packages (comfygit-core and comfygit) now always share the exact same version number
- CLI dependency changed from `comfygit-core>=X.Y.Z` to `comfygit-core==X.Y.Z` (exact pin)
- Automated publishing triggered on push to main when pyproject.toml changes
- AI-generated release summaries using Claude Haiku

## Why Lockstep Versioning

CLI is tightly coupled to core - it imports types, models, exceptions, and protocols directly. Independent versioning created risk of users running mismatched versions that could break at runtime.

Lockstep ensures:
- Both packages always have identical version numbers
- Single mental model for users ("I'm on version X.Y.Z")
- Atomic releases - both packages publish together or not at all

## Unified Publish Workflow

The new `publish.yml` workflow:
1. **Triggers** on push to main (pyproject.toml changes) or manual dispatch
2. **Validates** core and CLI versions match (fails fast if not)
3. **Checks PyPI** - skips quietly if version already published
4. **Publishes core** first
5. **Polls PyPI** until core is available (15s intervals, 5min timeout)
6. **Publishes CLI** (now safe since core dependency is on PyPI)
7. **Creates GitHub release** with AI-generated summary

## New Release Workflow

```bash
make bump-version VERSION=X.Y.Z
git add -A && git commit -m "Bump version to X.Y.Z"
git push origin main
# GitHub Actions handles publish + release automatically
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.github/workflows/publish.yml` | New unified workflow |
| `.github/workflows/publish-core.yml` | Deleted |
| `.github/workflows/publish-cli.yml` | Deleted |
| `packages/cli/pyproject.toml` | `>=` → `==` for core dependency |
| `Makefile` | `bump-version` updates exact pin |
| `dev/scripts/check-versions.py` | Enforces exact match |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Rewritten version management docs |
| `docs/codebase-map.md` | Updated architecture notes |

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `make check-versions` passes
- [ ] Verify `make bump-version VERSION=X.Y.Z` updates all files correctly
- [ ] After merge, verify workflow triggers and publishes successfully
- [ ] Add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret for AI-generated release summaries

## Summary

Build admin client assets during the GitHub Actions deployment workflow instead of committing them to source control.

## Changes

### Build Artifacts (.gitignore)
- Added `src/Goldfinch.Admin/Client/dist/*` to .gitignore
- Removed previously committed dist file from git tracking

### GitHub Actions Workflow (deploy.yml)
- Added Node.js admin client build steps before .NET build:
  - Install admin client dependencies (`npm ci`)
  - Build admin client assets (`npm run build`)
- Steps run in `src/Goldfinch.Admin/Client` directory

### Node Version Standardization
- Added `.nvmrc` file specifying Node 22
- Added `engines` field to package.json requiring Node >=22

### Package Version Alignment
- Updated Kentico npm packages to match NuGet package versions (30.12.0):
  - `@kentico/xperience-admin-base`: 30.9.2 → 30.12.0
  - `@kentico/xperience-admin-components`: 30.9.2 → 30.12.0
  - `@kentico/xperience-webpack-config`: 30.9.2 → 30.12.0

## Benefits

1. **Cleaner Repository**: Built artifacts no longer committed to source control
2. **Fresh Builds**: Client assets are built fresh on every deployment
3. **Version Consistency**: npm packages now match NuGet package versions (30.12.0)
4. **Consistent Environments**: `.nvmrc` ensures same Node version across all environments

## Testing

- ✅ Admin client build succeeds (`npm run build`)
- ✅ .NET build succeeds with built client assets
- ✅ Deployment workflow will build assets before .NET build

author: vdimarco
body:
## Summary
- Enhances track_referral_signup to handle existing referrals and conflicting codes with an idempotent path.
- Enforces referral code usage limits, preventing duplicate pending records and ensuring referred_by_code is synced on the referred user.
- Adds robust logging and error handling for edge cases and update failures.

## Changes

### Backend
- In track_referral_signup:
  - Check for an existing referral for the referred_user_id BEFORE applying usage limits
  - If an existing referral exists:
    - If the existing code equals the provided referral_code:
      - Ensure referred_by_code is set on the referred user (idempotent)
    - Else:
      - Do not modify records and return a descriptive error to prevent changing the referral association
  - If no existing referral exists:
    - Check the referral_code usage against MAX_REFERRAL_USES
    - If usage limit is reached:
      - Return a descriptive error to prevent over-use
    - Create a pending referral record with:
      - referrer_id, referred_user_id, referral_code, bonus_amount, status="pending", created_at
    - Ensure the creation result is successful
  - After handling creation or conflict, update the referred_user_id’s user record with referred_by_code
  - Emit logs for:
    - Detection of existing referral
    - Conflict when codes differ
    - Successful tracking
    - Failure to update referred_by_code

### Data Integrity & Logging
- Prevents duplicate referral records for the same referred_user_id
- Keeps referral metadata in sync with user stats via referred_by_code
- Adds informative logging to aid debugging and monitoring of referral flows
- Adds edge-case handling for conflicting codes and logs appropriate warnings

### Test plan
- [x] Create a new referral: verify a pending referral is created and referred_by_code is set on the referred user
- [x] Re-signup with the same referred_user_id: verify no new referral record is created, but referred_by_code is updated and an info log is emitted
- [x] Validate referral stats page shows the referred user under the referrer after referred_by_code is set
- [x] Simulate user update failure: verify a warning is logged and system remains stable
- [x] New: Re-signup with a conflicting referral_code for the same referred_user_id should fail gracefully with no changes

## Notes
- No frontend logic changes were required for this update; backend changes ensure referral data consistency and accurate stats on the referral page.
- 📎 **Task**: https://www.terragonlabs.com/task/17bb93d7-1888-4783-8ae4-f086da80f2dc
